oneLiner.en: Through the Maharal, the Mashgiach explains that Rachel, the akeres habayis who gathers Klal Yisrael, was buried on the road so that her power to gather goes with the Jews into exile, and he presents the kever of Shmuel and Chana as a place to pray for those who are spiritually barren and for the raising of the horn of Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach learns the Maharal on the Midrash that Yaakov buried Rachel on the road to Efras so she would ask mercy for her children in exile. A wife is called 'bayis' because the home gathers the scattered family, and Rachel was Yaakov's akeres habayis. The road scatters; since exile is a road, Rachel's gathering power goes with the Jews, and in her merit they return. He links this to Beis Lechem, the place of Moshiach. He then presents Sefer Devarim as the seventh book, the kallah, like Shabbos. At the kever of Shmuel and Chana he ties them to Rosh Hashanah, brings the Arizal on Shmuel's gilgulim, and calls the place a site to pray for the barren, for fruitful Torah and tefilah, and for Moshiach's horn. He closes on punctual Shabbos davening.

en: A wife is called 'bayis' because a home gathers and unites the scattered family, and Rachel was the akeres habayis of Yaakov.
Rachel was buried on the road, the opposite of a home, so that her gathering power would accompany the Jews on the road of exile.
In the merit of Rachel's gathering power the Jews will return from their exile, and her place near Beis Lechem is the place of Moshiach.
Shmuel and Chana are bound up with Rosh Hashanah: Chana's story is its haftorah and the laws of tefilah are learned from her.
The kever of Shmuel and Chana is a place to pray for the barren to be remembered, and also that one's Torah and tefilah not be 'barren' without fruit.
Shmuel brought kingship into the world, anointing Shaul from Rachel and David from Leah, so his place is fitting to pray for the raising of Moshiach's horn.
Shacharis is the main tefilah and sets the whole day, and the Shabbos morning davening sets the whole Shabbos, so one must come on time.

title.en: The Maharal: Rachel as akeres habayis

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens the Maharal on the Midrash about why Yaakov buried Rachel on the road to Efras, with the pesukim of Rachel weeping for her children. He explains that a wife is called 'bayis' because a home gathers the scattered family, and Rachel was Yaakov's akeres habayis.

title.en: Buried on the road, gathering the exiles

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the road is the opposite of a home, and Rachel was buried there so her gathering power goes with the Jews into exile; in her merit they return. He ties this to Shabbos Chazon and to Beis Lechem, the place of Moshiach, and speaks of praying at her kever.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Sefer Devarim, the seventh book and the kallah

summary.en: The Mashgiach counts Sefer Devarim as the seventh book, like Shabbos the seventh day, and calls both the kallah. Devarim begins on Shabbos Chazon, and he brings the passuk that Hashem does not despise Klal Yisrael in their enemies' land, for they are His kallah.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Shmuel, Chana and Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: After wishing for Shabbosos with proper davening, the Mashgiach turns to the kever of Shmuel and Chana and ties both to Rosh Hashanah. He brings the Arizal that Shmuel was a gilgul from Korach and later came back as Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, and the Gemara that Shmuel never took benefit from others.

title.en: Praying for the barren and for Moshiach's horn

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that Chana first called Hashem 'Tzevakos' and was one of the seven barren women, so her kever is a place for the barren to be remembered, and also to pray that one's Torah and tefilah not be barren. Since Shmuel anointed Shaul and David and Chana's song ends with the raising of Moshiach's horn, it is a place to pray for that too.

title.en: Coming on time to Shabbos Shacharis

summary.en: Pointing to the parsha of yirah in the week's sidra, the Mashgiach stresses coming on time to Shabbos morning davening: Shacharis sets the whole day and the whole Shabbos, the Arizal speaks of a stronger neshamah yeseirah on Shabbos morning, and the Shabbos mizmorim, brachos and Nishmas are entirely different from the weekday ones.

title.en: A story and the holiness of the beis medrash

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells a story involving poritzim and a lavish meal. He then speaks of the great kindness of having a holy beis medrash where great tzaddikim davened.

title.en: Davening in a holy place; Kedushah and the tish

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that a place where tzaddikim davened is a help to daven better, calls the Shabbos Kedushah of Keser the highest of the week, and says a Friday-night tish is a great thing but must not come at the expense of davening. He returns to Chana as the source of the laws of tefilah and closes asking for yiras shamayim.

catalogTitle: דברי התעוררות והדרכה להנוסעים לא"י לפורים משולש

oneLiner.en: Before a group journey to Eretz Yisroel for a Purim that falls on Shabbos, the Mashgiach explains the holiness of the land and of Purim in Yerushalayim, and guides the travelers on how to prepare, how to feel, and how to behave on the way and on Purim.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by calling Eretz Yisroel the 'eretz chemdah', the desired land, as Shabbos is the most desired of days, and contrasts the mesiras nefesh of earlier generations with today's easy travel. Hashem's eyes are always on the land, so living there or even visiting demands a cheshbon: holiness magnifies both merit and damage, as on Shabbos. He describes the Shabbos Purim of Yerushalayim, which only exists there, and through the Arizal explains why it spreads over three days. Tefillos are accepted in Eretz Yisroel, as shown from Yehoshua and Yaakov's fear of Esav. Through the Chasam Sofer he teaches that the land must be seen with different eyes, and shows that one day of Purim makes a person a resident of Yerushalayim. He warns not to be broken if the feeling does not come, with stories of tzaddikim, and closes with guidance on kiddush Hashem during the flight and a serious Purim without drunkenness.

en: Earlier generations reached Eretz Yisroel only with great mesiras nefesh, and great tzaddikim were held back from Heaven; today a large part of Klal Yisroel lives there and even a visit is not a waste of time.
Because Hashem's special providence rests on Eretz Yisroel, being there demands worthiness, and a traveler must make a cheshbon of why he is going.
The Purim that falls on Shabbos in Yerushalayim exists only there, and its power is so great that it spreads over three days.
Eretz Yisroel is the place where tefillos are accepted, which is why tzaddikim abroad would write there asking to be davened for.
One day of Purim in Yerushalayim makes a person a resident of the city with all its laws, although residency in Eretz Yisroel normally takes thirty days.
If one feels no special warmth in Eretz Yisroel he should not be broken: the feeling is a gift from Heaven, and sometimes Hashem asks for avodah without it.
On the way and on Purim the travelers must make a kiddush Hashem: quiet, courteous behavior on the airplane and a Purim with serious moments, not drunkenness.

candidateTopics: preparing for a trip to Eretz Yisroel

title.en: The desired land and the mesiras nefesh of old

summary.en: The Mashgiach says he will review known matters before the trip. He explains 'eretz chemdah', the land the Avos desired, as Shabbos is the most desired of days, recalls Moshe Rabbeinu's many tefillos to enter and Dovid's love for its very stones, and contrasts today's comfortable flight with the dangerous journeys of earlier generations and the Ramban, who left family and students to come.

title.en: Held back then, let in now

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Gra had to turn back midway and how the Chofetz Chaim's packed bags stayed home when his rebbetzin fell ill, while today a third of Klal Yisroel lives in the land and a visit is no waste of time. From the passuk that Hashem's eyes are on the land all year he explains its special providence, and says that living there is a serious undertaking that requires being worthy.

title.en: Entering a holy place with preparation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Yerushalayim was meant for coming three times a year to strengthen one's yiras Shamayim, and that one must prepare for Eretz Yisroel as for entering a beis medrash, since a street there is holier than a shul abroad. He tells that the Chasam Sofer did not go but urged his talmidim to, and brings his words that the land makes a tzaddik greater, while its wicked become worse.

title.en: Greater holiness, greater responsibility

summary.en: Comparing the land to Shabbos, when a blatt Gemara is holier and a sin graver, the Mashgiach explains that in Eretz Yisroel one receives a different neshamah, brings the Gemara's levels of four amos, thirty days and a full year, and compares a careless visitor to one entering the king's court in sackcloth. Therefore one must make a cheshbon before going and not travel merely for sightseeing.

title.en: Shabbos Purim in Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes a Shabbos and Nishmas in Eretz Yisroel and the Purim that falls on Shabbos, which can only be kept in Yerushalayim. Through the Arizal's explanation of why chutz la'aretz needs two days of Yom Tov, he shows why this Purim spreads over three days, and then explains that Eretz Yisroel is the place where tefillos are accepted.

title.en: The zechus of Eretz Yisroel

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Yehoshua was punished for not davening away the yetzer hara of avodah zarah, and explains why Moshe Rabbeinu could not do it while Yehoshua could: he was in Eretz Yisroel. He adds the Ramak's teaching that the land is surrounded by water on four sides, and Chazal's explanation that Yaakov feared Esav because of his kibbud av and the zechus of living in the land.

title.en: Decrees undone and the signs of desire

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that one sentenced abroad who flees to Eretz Yisroel is judged again, since a merit may be found for him there, and Avraham Avinu's years in the land, to show that decrees can be undone there. He cites the Sefer Chareidim on longing for the land, gives two signs of spiritual sickness, lacking desire to learn and to go to Eretz Yisroel, and tells the travelers to examine whether they long for the trip or for its holiness.

title.en: Seeing the land with different eyes

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer that the earth of Eretz Yisroel is holier than the heavens of chutz la'aretz, and compares looking at the land to looking at a Jew and a goy: the same outward form, an entirely different thing. He mentions Dovid HaMelech's pride that his feet stood in Yerushalayim, and quotes the Chasam Sofer in Parshas Shelach that one who understands the holiness of the land and of his soul would give everything just to see it.

title.en: One day of Purim makes a citizen

summary.en: The Mashgiach cautions against going into debt for the trip, then recalls the three levels of settling the land and that residency normally requires thirty days. On Purim, however, one day in Yerushalayim makes a person a resident of a walled city with all its laws, just as being in the land for the seven days of Sukkos suffices because dwelling in a sukkah for seven days counts as dwelling.

title.en: The Kosel, the prophets and the Shabbos of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Maharal and Sfas Emes that Purim in Yerushalayim is far greater, and the Arvei Nachal that in galus all the holiness of the Beis Hamikdash is concentrated in the Kosel. From the Gemara that every place grows its own plants he shows that Yerushalayim grows nevi'im, explains that the power of Purim spreads beyond the old city, and teaches that Mordechai and Esther originally instituted reading the Megillah on Shabbos, so the whole power of this Purim rests in its Shabbos.

title.en: When the feeling does not come

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the travelers to prepare in the weeks before the trip by learning with more diligence and davening better, and not to be shaken if in Eretz Yisroel they feel a blocked heart. He explains that a sweet feeling in Torah and tefillah is 'avodas matanah', a gift from Heaven, brings the Ohr HaChaim on how intense the true pleasure of Torah is, and says that sometimes Hashem asks for labor without the gift.

title.en: Two tefillos that felt dry

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of R' Avraham Kalisker's letters from Eretz Yisroel, where he concluded that his first, dry tefillah there was greater than a famous minchah under a tree, and of R' Sholom of Prohobisht, whose strained Erev Rosh Hashanah minchah brought tikkun to thousands of souls, as R' Nachum of Chernobyl told him. He concludes that one should ask for a feeling in the land but not be disappointed without it.

title.en: Kiddush Hashem on the airplane

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks the bachurim and yungeleit to make a kiddush Hashem on the flight: no shouting, no trouble for the crew, and saying thank you, as he illustrates from the custom in Oberland of kissing one's mother's hand after a meal. He reports that rabbanim now say not to block the aisles with minyanim but to daven seated, distinguishes between halachah and a chumra that must be weighed, and urges helping others with their baggage.

title.en: A serious Purim and a tefillah for the journey

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns against wild behavior and drunkenness on Purim, distinguishing the Satmar Rav's holy intoxication from ordinary people, and brings the Rambam, the Meiri and the Mishnah Berurah on drinking a little and going to sleep. He recalls R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz insisting on a serious moment at the Purim seudah, brings R' Zeira who crossed the Yarden on a rope bridge lest he lose the chance, and ends with a tefillah that the journey succeed.

catalogTitle: שמשון הגיבור - הוא נוקם כנגד הפאליסטינער בגלל יהודים שבעיקבתא דמשיחא (יארצייט של סקולענר רבי זצ”ל) שמעון הצדיק - שיריים של אנשי כנה"ג. קבר רחל - ווי לאנג וועט זי וויינען!?

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shimshon's strength lay in his hair, which stands for the lowest, cut-off Jews of the generation before Moshiach, and that Shimshon's prayer and his war against the Plishtim continue in that generation.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the teaching that Yaakov, blessing Dan, saw Shimshon and thought he was Moshiach, then saw him fall and said 'lishuascha kivisi Hashem'. Chazal seem to contradict themselves about Shimshon; the Mashgiach explains that Shimshon went down to assimilating Jews to pull them out, with intent for Heaven. His strength was in his hair, the lowest parts of Klal Yisroel, Dan being the last tribe. The nazir's hair is a crown, 'nezer Elokav al rosho', the gematria of ikvesa d'meshicha: the last Jews will become the crown. He connects Shimshon's war against the Plishtim, his prayer 'zochreini na' and his destruction of Aza to the Palestinians of today, and calls on the listeners to daven with Shimshon. After prayer and a niggun, he speaks briefly about Shimon HaTzaddik.

en: Shimshon went down to the lowest levels, to assimilating Jews, in order to pull them out, and his intent was for the sake of Heaven.
Shimshon's strength was in his hair, which stands for the lowest Jews who are cut off from Klal Yisroel, the Jews of ikvesa d'meshicha.
The lowest and last Jews, the generation before Moshiach, will become the crown of Klal Yisroel and the greatest tzaddikim.
The Palestinians take their name from the Plishtim, and a name defines a thing, so Shimshon's war against the Plishtim continues against them.
Yaakov's prayer 'lishuascha kivisi Hashem' was for the generation of ikvesa d'meshicha, that through their tefillos they should hold out through the last moments of the exile.
Shimon HaTzaddik, one of the remnants of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, is the first named in the chain of the Oral Torah after Moshe and led the Jews into the era of the Tanna'im.

title.en: Yaakov sees Shimshon; Shimshon's descent

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the teaching that Yaakov saw Shimshon and thought he was Moshiach, notes the apparent contradictions in Chazal about Shimshon, and explains that Shimshon went down to the lowest Jews to pull them out, with intent for Heaven. His strength was in his hair, and when it was cut his strength left him.

title.en: The hair: the last Jews as the crown

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the cut-off hair stands for the lost Jews of the generation before Moshiach, whom Hashem's tzaddikim raise up. The nazir's hair is a crown, and 'nezer Elokav al rosho' is the gematria of ikvesa d'meshicha; hair is the last thing to develop in a fetus, so the last generation completes Klal Yisroel.

title.en: Shimshon's revenge and the Palestinians

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Shimshon's prayer 'zochreini na' and his wish to take revenge on the Plishtim even at the cost of his life. He explains that the Palestinians are named after the Plishtim, and a name defines a thing, so Shimshon's war against them continues.

title.en: Yaakov's prayer and joining Shimshon's tefilah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Yaakov saw in Shimshon the soul that is the root of the generation of ikvesa d'meshicha and prayed for them 'lishuascha kivisi Hashem'. He recalls Shimshon's destruction of Aza, contrasts it with today, and calls on the listeners to daven together with Shimshon for revenge and for Eretz Yisroel and Yerushalayim to be for Jews.

title.en: Tefilah and a niggun

summary.en: A short prayer that the tefilah be accepted, followed by chanting of 'zochreinu' and a long stretch of singing, including a niggun attributed to the Skulener Rebbe.

title.en: Shimon HaTzaddik, remnant of the Knesses HaGedolah

summary.en: The Mashgiach mentions that Shimon HaTzaddik prevented Alexander from destroying Yerushalayim, and explains that being one of the 'remnants' of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah is like the shirayim of a Rebbe that connect people to him. Shimon HaTzaddik is the first named in the chain of the Oral Torah after Moshe and opened the era of the Tanna'im.

catalogTitle: Recognizing Hashem Through the Wonders of the Torah

oneLiner.en: Turning from the wonders of creation to the wonders of the Torah, the Mashgiach shows from its endless depth, the wisdom contained in it, its fulfilled promises and the survival of the Jewish people with their Torah that the Torah is from Heaven.

abstract.en: After earlier weeks on the wonders of creation, the Mashgiach turns to the wonders of the Torah. A man-made work, a poem or a painting, is exhausted once understood, and a schoolboy discards each year's books; yet the same Chumash and the same Eilu Metziyos serve a child, a bochur and the greatest gedolim, each finding more depth, just as scientists never finish discovering nature. Everything is in the Torah: he tells how the Ramban showed his student Avner, who had become a heretic, his own name in Ha'azinu, and how the Chazon Ish guided surgeons and said everything is in the Torah. He then shows the Torah's promises fulfilled: the conquest by Yehoshua, the division of the land by lottery as Yaakov and Moshe foretold, the protection of property during aliyah l'regel, and above all the survival of the Jewish people and their Torah through a long exile while their oppressors vanished.

en: A man-made wisdom is exhausted once understood, but the same Chumash and Gemara reveal ever more depth to a child, a bochur and the greatest gedolim, which shows the Torah is Divine wisdom.
Like nature, which scientists never finish exploring because Hashem made it, the Torah is endless.
Everything is in the Torah: the Sages knew all the wisdoms, such as agriculture, astronomy and geometry, from the Torah, and the Mashgiach saw this in his own time in the Chazon Ish.
The Torah's promises, written down before they happened, were fulfilled to the letter: Yehoshua's conquest, the division of the land by lottery, and the safety of property during aliyah l'regel.
The survival of the Jewish people in a long exile, while all their mighty oppressors disappeared, and the living Torah learning of today, are a wonder that shows the Torah is from Heaven.

title.en: From wonders of creation to wonders of Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach turns from the wonders of creation to the wonders of the Torah, which a deep learner sees show it is not man-made. He contrasts a poem or a painting, which yields nothing new on rereading, and a schoolboy who must replace his books every year.

title.en: The same Chumash and Eilu Metziyos, ever deeper

summary.en: A child in cheder keeps the same Chumash and later the same Eilu Metziyos as a bochur, an old man and the gedolim, each seeing more depth. The Mashgiach compares this to nature, which scientists never finish discovering because Hashem made it.

title.en: The Ramban and Avner: everything is in Ha'azinu

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the story of the Ramban's student Avner, who became a heretic because he could not believe that everyone is alluded to in Ha'azinu, and how the Ramban showed him his name in the third letters of four words of a passuk there.

title.en: All wisdoms are in the Torah: the Chazon Ish

summary.en: Citing the Ramban's introduction to Chumash, the Mashgiach explains that the Sages knew all the sciences from the Torah, and tells how the Chazon Ish guided surgeons in America and told an astonished surgeon that everything is in the Torah.

title.en: Promises of the Torah fulfilled

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows the Torah's truth from promises written in advance that came true: the land promised to the Avos, the Zohar on the round earth, Yehoshua's conquest, the lottery that matched what Yaakov and Moshe told each shevet, and the safety of fields during the three pilgrimages.

title.en: The wonder of Jewish survival in exile

summary.en: Moshe foretold exile but promised the people would remain a nation; the Mashgiach shows how Rome, Greece and the other oppressors vanished while the Jews survived, even Hitler, and calls this a greater wonder than the Exodus. He ends with the promise that the Torah will not be forgotten, seen in the multitudes learning today.

catalogTitle: קבר רחל - להתפלל על גאולת רחל וירושלים בחינתה. מערת המכפלה

oneLiner.en: Speaking at Kever Rochel and at the Me'aras HaMachpelah, the Mashgiach calls for prayer for the redemption of Rochel and Yerushalayim, now surrounded by the 'uncircumcised and impure', and for the strength of Avraham Avinu's emunah, to stand alone against the whole world.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by thanking Hashem for the merit of davening Maariv at Kever Rochel. Rochel, he explains, is the aspect of Malchus, Shabbos, the Beis HaMikdash and Yerushalayim, which is why Tikkun Rochel at Tikkun Chatzos mourns Yerushalayim. He connects Rochel's words at Yosef's birth, 'Hashem has taken away my disgrace', to the disgrace of orlah, Esav who was never circumcised against Yosef who was born circumcised. He tells the Midrash of the maiden who fled the corruption before the Flood on an angel's wing and became the mazal of Elul, and urges grabbing Elul's opportunities. From the haftorah of Nachamu he describes Rochel and Yerushalayim surrounded by Yishmael, 'arel v'tamei', and calls for prayer for their redemption. At the Me'aras HaMachpelah he speaks of Avraham, one against the world, and Kalev, one against the spies, and asks for strength in today's tests of emunah. He closes with Tu B'Av, the coming joy of chassan and kallah, and accepting emunah.

en: Rochel is the aspect of Malchus, Shabbos, the Beis HaMikdash and Yerushalayim; Tikkun Rochel at Tikkun Chatzos is the mourning over Yerushalayim.
Elul is a month that can be 'grabbed', as the maiden and Yaakov grabbed it, and every Jew should seize its opportunities for Torah, mitzvos and chesed.
Kever Rochel, like Yerushalayim, the root of Rochel, is now surrounded by Yishmael, the 'arel v'tamei', and one must pray for Mother Rochel to be freed from them.
Like Avraham against the whole world and Kalev against the spies, an upright Jew today must hold to holy views even when he stands alone.
All prayers pass through the place of the Avos, which is why Shemoneh Esrei opens with 'the G-d of Avraham, the G-d of Yitzchak, the G-d of Yaakov'; there one should pray for emunah.
Tu B'Av begins the joy of the union of Hashem with Knesses Yisrael, like chassan and kallah, which will be complete when Moshiach comes.

title.en: Rochel, Yerushalayim and the disgrace of orlah

summary.en: The Mashgiach thanks Hashem for the merit of davening Maariv at Kever Rochel and explains that Rochel is the aspect of Malchus, Shabbos and Yerushalayim. He then reads Rochel's words at Yosef's birth with Rashi and ties her 'disgrace' to orlah: Esav was never circumcised, while Yosef was born circumcised.

title.en: The maiden on the angel's wing and Elul

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells a Midrash: before the Flood a maiden, afraid of the corruption, grabbed the wing of a fallen angel, flew to the Kisei HaKavod and was made the mazal of Elul. He concludes that Elul is a month to grab, and that Kever Rochel is a place to pray for protection in the days before Moshiach.

title.en: Rochel surrounded by the 'arel v'tamei'

summary.en: From the haftorah of Nachamu and the promise that the 'arel v'tamei' will no longer enter Yerushalayim, the Mashgiach describes Kever Rochel and Yerushalayim surrounded by Yishmael, whose milah does not remove his orlah, since he is the greatest ba'al ta'avah. He calls for prayer for Mother Rochel and ends with the pesukim of Rochel weeping for her children and their return.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude between the talk at Kever Rochel and the talk at the Me'aras HaMachpelah.

title.en: Avraham and Kalev: one against all

summary.en: At the Me'aras HaMachpelah the Mashgiach brings 'Look to Avraham your father … for he was one' and the Midrash that Avraham stood alone against the whole world. He cites the early disciples of the Ba'al Shem Tov that before Moshiach a Jew will look around for scoffers before saying a warm word to Hashem, and explains that Kalev drew strength here to stand alone against the spies; so too today one must hold to holy views alone.

title.en: Praying through the Avos for emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks Hashem, as Magen Avraham, to protect us as He protected Avraham, the root of Klal Yisrael who passed the tests up to the Akeidah. He says the main war of Gog and Magog will be against emunah, that all prayers pass through this place, which is why Shemoneh Esrei begins with the Avos, and that here one should pray to be saved from false views and false leaders.

title.en: Tu B'Av, chassan and kallah, and accepting emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that today is Tu B'Av, which begins the preparation for Shemini Atzeres and the joy of Hashem's union with Knesses Yisrael, like chassan and kallah, as in the last of the seven haftoros of consolation. He brings Kapitel 89 of Tehillim, which Chazal attribute to Avraham, on planting emunah in all generations, and closes by having the people accept emunah and recite the principles of faith, with the Midrash that Jews will leave galus in the merit of emunah.

catalogTitle: קבר רחל - אין עמלק נופל אלא ביד בניה של רחל

oneLiner.en: Speaking at Kever Rachel before Purim, the Mashgiach explains that Rachel, the mother who unites Klal Yisroel, is the root of Purim and of the war against Amalek, and that the growing concealment of her grave is a sign of the final hester before the revelation.

abstract.en: After a tefilah and a short blessing, the Mashgiach says that the light Yaakov Avinu placed in Rachel's matzeivah is still present, and recalls that the Imrei Emes davened there with Yaakov's intentions. Rachel is the akeres habayis who unites Klal Yisroel, and the thirteenth of Adar is a 'zman kehilah', a time of gathering. Following the Gemara, Purim came through Rachel's tznius in giving Leah the signs, and Amalek falls only through Rachel's children, through Moshiach ben Yosef, after which comes Moshiach ben Dovid. Her mesirus nefesh for her sister and for Binyamin, the root of Mordechai, made her the mother of Purim. Rachel still weeps over her children and Hashem still comforts her. Rachel is the revealed one, yet her grave has become covered by walls: a sign of hester within hester at the end of galus, which Purim, the megillah of hester, comes to reveal.

en: The lights and intentions that Yaakov Avinu, Yosef and the shevatim placed in Rachel's matzeivah remain there to this day.
Rachel is the akeres habayis and mother of Klal Yisroel who unites all of it, which is why her grave stands open on the road for all to reach.
Purim came about because of Rachel's tznius in handing the signs to Leah, which earned Shaul and through him Esther.
Amalek falls only by the hand of Rachel's children, through Moshiach ben Yosef, after which Moshiach ben Dovid comes.
Rachel still weeps for her children, and Hashem still comforts her that the children will return to their border.
The walls now surrounding Kever Rachel, whose grave should be revealed, are a sign of hester within hester at the end of galus, which Purim comes to reveal.

candidateTopics: Rachel imeinu as mother of Klal Yisroel
Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben Dovid
hester panim at the end of galus
revealed and hidden: Rachel and Leah

title.en: Tefilah at Kever Rachel and opening blessing

summary.en: A tefilah for Klal Yisroel is recited at the grave. The Mashgiach then blesses those present with yeshuos and hatzlachos and with the true war against Amalek that precedes the building of the Beis Hamikdash.

title.en: Yaakov's matzeivah and Rachel the uniting mother

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the lights Yaakov placed in Rachel's matzeivah are still there, recalling how the Imrei Emes davened there with Yaakov's intentions. Rachel is the akeres habayis who unites Klal Yisroel, and the thirteenth of Adar, a 'zman kehilah', is the fitting day to gather at her grave.

title.en: Amalek falls only by Rachel's children

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Purim came through Rachel's tznius in giving the signs, and the teaching that Amalek falls only by Rachel's children, through Moshiach ben Yosef. He explains how her mesirus nefesh for her sister and for Binyamin, the root of Mordechai, made her the mother of Purim.

title.en: Rachel weeps, Hashem comforts; revealed and hidden

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads 'Rachel mevakah al baneha' as an ongoing weeping that Hashem still answers with 'veshavu banim ligvulam', and ties the joy of Adar to that consolation. He then contrasts Rachel, the aspect of revelation, with Leah, the aspect of concealment, in their marriages and their graves.

title.en: The covered grave: hester within hester

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares the holiness spreading through Rachel's ohel to the halacha of an ohel, then tells of the Munkatcher Rav's fast over the building Sir Moses Montefiore put over the grave. Answering with bechirah and yediah, he sees today's walls as the lowest hester of the end of galus, which Purim, the megillah of hester, comes to reveal, and closes with a blessing for the geulah.

catalogTitle: חובתו בעולמו; תפילה היא העיקר בזמן הזה; עבודה שבלב

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches bochurim that a Jew's whole life belongs to the service of Hashem, and that in our generation the main avodah is tefillah, davened with the heart and with time.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by calling the beis medrash a place of tefillah and lays the foundation from the first chapter of Mesilas Yesharim: a person must know his duty in his world. Serving Hashem is not a tax paid three times a day; eating, sleeping, earning a living and even exercise are part of the avodah when done for that purpose, as the Rambam's hired worker who sharpens his axe is paid for the whole day. He then turns to tefillah, which Chazal say people belittle. Torah is greater, yet its study is mixed with incentives, while tefillah is pure speech to Hashem; in the era before Moshiach, as the Ba'al Shem Tov taught, tefillah is the main avodah. Tefillah must be avodah of the heart: knowing the words, taking time, saying each word like counting money. He recalls how Jews once davened and announces a program of learning the meaning of davening.

en: A person must know his duty in his world: his entire life, every hour of the day, is meant for the service of Hashem.
Physical needs such as eating, sleeping and rest become part of avodas Hashem when done with that intent, and are revealed retroactively as such when the person then turns to serving Hashem.
Tefillah is a great avodah that people belittle and do not value.
Although Torah is the greater avodah, in our time, the era before Moshiach, the main avodah is tefillah.
Tefillah must be avodah of the heart: knowing what one says, turning to Hashem, and taking enough time.
The Mashgiach announces that the beis medrash will learn the meaning of the words of davening, beginning with a few weeks on the importance of tefillah.

candidateTopics: a person's duty in his world
tefillah as the main avodah in our time

title.en: A place of tefillah; a person's duty in his world

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the bochurim that their yeshivos are places of Torah and this beis medrash a place of tefillah, and opens with the foundation from Mesilas Yesharim that a person must know his duty in his world. Avodas Hashem is not like paying taxes for set times; a Jew's whole life is devoted to it.

title.en: Eating and sleeping as part of avodah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that eating, sleeping, earning a living and even exercise are for avodas Hashem, like the Rambam's worker whose axe-sharpening counts as work. If after his physical needs a person does not turn to Torah, it shows he did them for himself.

title.en: Tefillah, the belittled avodah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says davening is a great avodah people do not recognize, and brings the Gemara that tefillah stands at the height of the world yet people belittle it. He tells how Reb Nochum of Chernobyl davened over a quarrel with a maid, since everything one needs must be asked of Hashem.

title.en: Torah is greater, yet tefillah is the main avodah now

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets the order: Torah, then tefillah, then the other mitzvos. Yet Torah study draws many incentives, and the Toldos Yaakov Yosef writes that the Ba'al Shem Tov came mainly to strengthen tefillah; from the Arizal's time, the era before Moshiach, the main avodah is tefillah.

title.en: The sick man's diet; tefillah's purity and kavanah

summary.en: With a mashal of a sick man who cannot eat bread and meat and must live on oranges, the Mashgiach explains why a weak generation needs tefillah. Torah lishmah is hard and mixed with motives, but tefillah is pure speech to Hashem; davening without kavanah fulfills the rabbinic obligation but not 'with all your heart'.

title.en: Avodah of the heart takes time

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tefillah must come from the heart: Gemara is to be learned, davening is to be davened. It needs preparation and time; one cannot daven in twenty minutes, and he brings the Magen Avraham and the Shulchan Aruch on how long Pesukei Dezimra should take and saying words like counting money.

title.en: How Jews used to daven

summary.en: The Mashgiach recalls an old chassid who davened word by word like counting money, contrasts today's hurried minyanim in the shtiblach with how simple Jews once davened, and describes the Satmar Rav davening slowly and aloud with the bochurim. He brings the Gemara that one who lengthens his tefillah has his days lengthened.

title.en: The chassidim harishonim and the beis medrash's aim

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik's pity for young men who never saw a Jew's avodah in davening, and brings the Gemara that the early chassidim spent nine hours a day on tefillah and their Torah was preserved. He explains the beis medrash wants to renew what was forgotten and announces learning the meaning of davening.

title.en: An old world needs tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts earlier generations, when Torah alone sufficed, with today, when the world is old and bent over and the main avodah is tefillah. He tells the bochurim that their years are for Torah, yet they must give davening its proper importance, and mentions the Yesod HaAvodah of Reb Avraham of Slonim.

catalogTitle: “ולגדלתו אין חקר”- The Human Mind is not Capable of Understanding G-dliness

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why chakirah, philosophy, is a dangerous and unreliable path to emunah: the human mind is not the organ that grasps Hashem, while the neshamah, a part of G-d above, can feel Him unless aveiros insulate it.

abstract.en: After reviewing two approaches to emunah, inherited faith and seeing Hashem's wonders, the Mashgiach turns to a third, chakirah or philosophy. He notes that yeshivos learn the Rambam's halachos but not his Moreh Nevuchim, and explains why: philosophy is mental acrobatics, and a sharper mind can always refute a proof. Jewish philosophy arose in Arab lands to keep Jews from Greek thought, but the Gedolei Yisrael rejected it, and the Mashgiach tells how Rabbeinu Yonah, after Gemaras were burned in Paris, did teshuvah for his part in burning the Rambam's sefer. The mind, made of flesh, cannot grasp the Creator, as a watch cannot understand the watchmaker; the organ for that is the neshamah and nevuah, which aveiros insulate. Philosophy exposes a person to the kasha without the teretz. He closes with the Spanish expulsion, where simple Jews gave their lives while the philosophers converted.

en: Philosophy proves nothing, because any logical proof can be refuted by a sharper mind.
The Gedolei Yisrael of Ashkenaz never took to philosophy; it was a foreign import, while the Torah was received at Sinai.
The human mind, made of flesh, grasps only what is earthly and cannot understand Hashem, just as a watch cannot understand the watchmaker.
Hashem is perceived through a sixth sense, nevuah and ruach hakodesh, which every Jew has through his neshamah according to his level.
Aveiros insulate the neshamah and deaden its feeling, and teshuvah restores it.
Philosophy is dangerous because a person may grasp the kasha without the teretz, and even while weighing both sides he is for that moment not believing.

title.en: A third approach: philosophy

summary.en: The Mashgiach reviews the two earlier approaches to emunah and introduces a third, chakirah. He notes that yeshivos learn the Rambam's halachos but not his Moreh Nevuchim, and explains that philosophy is mental acrobatics that a sharper mind can always refute, so it proves nothing.

title.en: Gedolei Yisrael and Rabbeinu Yonah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Jewish philosophy was written in Arab lands to shield Jews from Greek philosophy, while the Gedolei Yisrael rejected it as a human product. He tells how Rabbeinu Yonah, after Gemaras were burned in Paris, did teshuvah for his role in burning the Rambam's sefer and wrote Shaarei Teshuvah.

title.en: The mind is not the organ for G-dliness

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem cannot be proven by logic because He is above the mind, which is made of flesh and understands only the earthly. A watch cannot understand its watchmaker, and claiming to understand Hashem with the mind is like listening to a painting or watching a symphony.

title.en: The neshamah's sixth sense and aveiros

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the sixth sense for knowing Hashem is ruach hakodesh and nevuah, which every Jew has through his neshamah. Aveiros wrap the neshamah like insulation on a wire or Novocaine in the gums, and teshuvah brings the feeling back.

title.en: A guide for the perplexed, and the kasha without the teretz

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the Ramchal's Mesillas Yesharim with the Rambam's Moreh Nevuchim, written for those who are lost and cannot yet be lit by Torah. He explains that the Gedolim discouraged philosophy because one may hear the kasha without the teretz, and shows from Ein K'Elokeinu that we say the answer before the question.

title.en: The expulsion from Spain

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells from the Or HaChaim of Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz that at the expulsion from Spain, on Tisha B'Av, simple Jews and women gave their lives for emunah, while those steeped in philosophy converted. He concludes that philosophy is a dangerous path to emunah and should be rejected, and promises a fourth approach next time.

catalogTitle: ראשית עריסותיכם חלה תרימו לה'

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach tells bachurim that the signs of Moshiach are all around, and that by sanctifying the beginning of each day with zeal, guarded speech before davening, tevilah with hope for the geulah and learning Torah with reverence, they hasten their own tikkun and the redemption.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the signs Chazal give for the coming of Moshiach, comparing the present state of the world to heavy clouds with thunder and lightning before rain. There are set times when the redemption is more likely, and a final time when it must come; by every sign this period is especially ripe. Mishnayos, tefillah, tzedakah and teshuvah bring Moshiach, and since Hashem acts measure for measure, a bachur who hurries to davening and learning awakens Heaven to bring the yeshuah early. Each soul is sent down for its tikkun, and one who comes early is rectified early. The Sanzer Rav's story of the torn bekeshe shows how a garment of mitzvos riddled with excuses falls apart. The beginning must be holy: the first words of the morning, no idle talk before davening, tevilah with hope for Moshiach, and Torah learned with reverence.

en: Chazal gave signs of Moshiach so that when people see them fulfilled they know the redemption is very near, and the Mashgiach compares the world's present turmoil to heavy clouds with thunder and lightning before rain.
Hashem runs the world measure for measure, so one who hurries to davening and learning without postponing awakens Heaven to bring the yeshuah early and not delay it.
Every soul is sent into the world to complete its tikkun, and one who comes early to davening and learning reaches his tikkun early, while one who is late delays it.

Every beginning must be sanctified, as Hashem sanctified the firstborn and the first fruits, because everything that follows is drawn after the beginning; the morning is like Rosh Hashanah of the day.
Idle talk before davening, over coffee or in the mikvah, spoils the davening, while words of chesed and chizuk to another Jew are a form of tzedakah.
Torah must be learned with reverence, aware whose Torah it is, and not casually or with levity, since the blessing over Torah says that Hashem sanctified us through it.

candidateTopics: the garment of mitzvos in Gan Eden

title.en: Clouds and thunder before the rain of geulah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the world is in turmoil and brings Chazal's signs of Moshiach, such as kingdoms provoking one another. He explains why the signs were given, that tzaddikim were shown propitious times for the redemption, and compares the present to heavy clouds with thunder and lightning before rain.

title.en: The final time and what brings Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach distinguishes the final time of 'be'itah', when Moshiach must come, from earlier times of 'achishenah', and says by all the signs this period is especially ripe. He lists the merits that bring Moshiach: Mishnayos and Gemara, tefillah, and tzedakah, which for a bachur means time and encouragement for a downcast friend.

title.en: Coming early: measure for measure and the soul's tikkun

summary.en: After teshuvah, the Mashgiach explains that Hashem acts measure for measure, so hurrying to davening and learning awakens an early redemption. Each soul comes down for its tikkun, and one who comes early is rectified early; Hashem is one's shadow, and real bachurim do not live on excuses.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the rotten bekeshe

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man who came to the Sanzer Rav for Yom Tov in a new bekeshe of cheap rotten silk that tore at every touch, and of the Sanzer Rav's remark that this is how a person looks in the next world. He explains that the mitzvos weave the soul's garment in Gan Eden and Torah is its food, so excuses leave the garment in tatters.

title.en: Sanctifying every beginning

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem sanctified the first in many mitzvos, the firstborn and the first fruits, and called Yisroel 'reishis', because all that follows is drawn after the beginning. So the beginning of the day, week, year and zman must be holy: the first words in the morning are Modeh Ani, and the morning is the Rosh Hashanah of the day, not a time for idle chatter.

title.en: No idle talk before davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the habit of chatting over coffee and in the mikvah before davening, which the Toldos and other sefarim say spoils the davening, and urges the bachurim to try not speaking. Speech for chesed or chizuk is different; it is a form of tzedakah, and the mikvah should be brief and a real preparation for tefillah.

title.en: Tevilah in honor of Moshiach; purifying all creation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that hoping for the yeshuah is a foundation of faith according to the Rambam, and recommends immersing once in the morning in honor of Moshiach's coming, as one immerses in honor of Shabbos. He explains that a tevilah below purifies the root of the soul above, and that washing negel vasser, as the Derech Hashem writes, purifies all creation, since all Jews are bound together.

title.en: Learning Torah with reverence

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Heaven watches how bachurim learn, and that one should strive for the highest quality of learning. He decries scratching one's head or touching shoes mid-learning without washing, jokes and disrespect toward Rishonim such as Rabbeinu Tam, and learning sprawled with feet on the table, explaining from the blessing over Torah that Torah must sanctify a person. He closes that the same hour of learning and davening can be worth vastly more when done as an eved Hashem.

catalogTitle: ויחפרו בארות - של תורה ותפילה; וסתמום פלישתים - סכנת ליצנות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains Yitzchak's digging of wells as the avodah of toiling in Torah and tefillah until one reaches the 'living waters', and warns that the Plishtim who stopped up the wells stand for letzanus, the mockery that cools a person's fervor in davening.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the avodah of each of the Avos and turns to Yitzchak's digging of wells. Since Hashem created everything, holiness lies in every thing; great tzaddikim could serve Hashem with all of it, while ordinary people have the mitzvos. Yitzchak's wells were deeds with meaning, and a Jew must likewise dig in the Gemara until the Torah reveals wondrous things. The Plishtim who stopped up the wells were leitzim who dismiss everything as 'just wells', and their mockery cools the desire to daven with feeling. Through the Yaaros Devash's letter, the mockery of the Chofetz Chaim and of Dovid Hamelech, the Mashgiach shows that tefillah is the portion of a person's toil. He weighs dveikus against knowing the whole Torah, explains moments of closeness as preparation for learning, brings the levels of davening from Nishmas and the Beis Aharon, and asks the bochurim to daven with liveliness, ending with strengthening in Torah in Kislev.

en: Each of the Avos had his own avodah, and Yitzchak's was digging wells again and again.
A Jew's avodah is to dig and dig in Torah with a Gemara until he reaches the 'living waters' and the Torah reveals wondrous things; if nothing is revealed, he must dig longer and deeper.
The Plishtim who stopped up the wells were leitzim, and their mockery of learning and of long davening cools the desire for heartfelt tefillah.
The Yaaros Devash wrote that, beyond all his learning and work for the public, his portion from all his toil is the moment he stands before Hashem in tefillah, even when people laugh at him.
Moments of dveikus in tefillah, even a few times a year, do not take away from knowing the Torah; they are a preparation that makes a person's learning a different kind of Torah.
Ordinary people must daven with liveliness and excitement, at a comfortable pitch rather than shouting themselves hoarse.

title.en: The avodah of each of the Avos

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that each of the Avos had his own avodah: Avraham built altars, Yitzchak dug wells, Yaakov carved rods at the watering troughs. He announces that he will speak of Yitzchak's digging, and explains that because Hashem created everything, holiness lies in every part of creation.

title.en: Digging in Torah until the living waters

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's cup and table and a story of the Kotzker and the Chasam Sofer to show how great tzaddikim served Hashem with every thing, while we have the mitzvos. He explains that Yitzchak's wells were meaningful deeds, and that a Jew must dig in the Gemara until the Torah reveals wondrous things.

title.en: The Plishtim: the danger of letzanus

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Plishtim were leitzim whose jokes cool a bochur's learning and davening, citing the Midrash and the Kol Simchah: they called the wells 'just wells' and filled them with earth, the element of laziness. Yitzchak dug them again, which teaches toil in Torah and in tefillah.

title.en: The Yaaros Devash's letter on long davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads a letter in the Yaaros Devash: the Rav of Königsberg asked Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz about his long Shemoneh Esrei on Rosh Hashanah, and he answered that on weekdays his learning and public duties keep him from long davening, yet he is still in Shemoneh Esrei when the tzibur says Kedushah, and people laugh at him.

title.en: Tzaddikim mocked in their time; tefillah as one's portion

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that tzaddikim are mocked in their lifetime, with a story of young talmidim in Radin who did not go to hear the Chofetz Chaim. He returns to the Yaaros Devash's words that tefillah is his portion from all his toil, brings the same from the Brisker Rav, and shows from Tehillim that even Dovid Hamelech was mocked and kept davening.

title.en: Dveikus and knowing the whole Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls dveikus the greatest mitzvah and brings the Shulchan Aruch HaRav that one may interrupt learning for it, except that knowing the whole Torah comes first. He explains the dispute over what that knowledge means, through the Rambam and the Beis Yosef, and concludes that ordinary people may still pause for moments of dveikus in tefillah, Nishmas or zemiros.

title.en: Tefillah as a preparation for Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Gerrer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, learning Gemara with dveikus at the Knessia Gedolah, and explains that a person who has had a moment of closeness in tefillah learns afterward with joy and a different approach. He cites the Gemara that tefillah stands at the height of the world yet people treat it lightly.

title.en: Levels of davening: Nishmas and the Beis Aharon

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Vizhnitzer's reading of 'bepi yesharim' in Nishmas: the higher a person stands, the less physical motion his tefillah needs, and great tzaddikim could daven quickly with no outward sign. From the Beis Aharon he explains that tzaddikei emes are like seraphim, while others are like ofanim and chayos who rise only with a great noise.

title.en: Davening with liveliness; Kislev and Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks the bochurim to daven with warmth and excitement at a comfortable pitch, with a pleasant nusach, and tells of a bochur who answered a complaint about his loud davening by pointing to the crowd shouting at a baseball game. He closes by urging strengthening in Torah in Kislev, since the Chashmonaim had mesiras nefesh for Torah.

catalogTitle: Miracles Enlighten the Darkness of עוה”ז

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that we live in a 'teivel', a world of confusion and hester panim, where Hashem's occasional revelations through tzaddikim are like lightning on a dark night, and our task is to believe even without seeing.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach contrasts earlier generations, who saw open miracles from Yetzias Mitzrayim through the Beis HaMikdash, the Tannaim and later, with today's hester panim, which is our test of emunah. He brings the pasuk in Tehillim that Hashem's lightnings illuminated the 'teivel', and explains that teivel, one of the seven names of the earth, means confusion, as in the blemish 'tevallul' in Parshas Emor. Like a flash of lightning that shows a lost traveler the road on a dark, rainy night, Hashem sometimes lets tzaddikim reveal Him for a moment. He tells stories of tzaddikim who sensed what was hidden: the Slonimer Rebbe and the untoveled dishes, a gabbai and an untoveled knife, Rabbi Binyamin Diskin and a questionable chicken, and the Yeshuos Yaakov and a pancake made in a meat pan. He ends with the Kotzker Rebbe's answer to the Apta Rav, that believing is a higher level than seeing, and says our mission in this darkness is to believe.

en: Earlier generations saw open miracles, such as the ten miracles in the Beis HaMikdash, while today there is hester panim and our test is to have emunah without seeing.
The word 'teivel' in the pasuk of the lightnings means confusion, so the pasuk describes Hashem's lightning lighting up a world of confusion.
In today's hester panim tzaddikim are not given permission to show wonders as in earlier times, yet here and there a tzaddik does something that lights up the darkness for a moment.
Stories of tzaddikim who sensed untoveled vessels and forbidden food show that such people could see what is hidden.
Believing is a higher level than seeing, and the mission of our souls in this dark period is to believe in Hashem even though He disguises Himself.
