teivel as a world of confusion
the Kotzker Rebbe and the Apta Rav

title.en: Generations that saw miracles, and our hester panim

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Jews at Yetzias Mitzrayim, in the time of the Beis HaMikdash with its ten daily miracles, and in later generations saw open miracles, while today there is hester panim and our test is emunah. He introduces the pasuk in Tehillim that Hashem's lightnings illuminated the 'teivel'.

title.en: Teivel means confusion; the lightning on a dark night

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that teivel, one of the seven names of the earth, means confusion and mixture, as in the eye blemish 'tevallul' in Parshas Emor and the word used for forbidden unions. He gives the mashal of a traveler on a dark, rainy night whom a brief flash of lightning shows the road.

title.en: Glimpses through tzaddikim in a world of hiding

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies the pasuk: we live in a teivel of hester panim where the wicked do as they please, and tzaddikim are not given permission to show wonders as before, yet occasionally a tzaddik's act lights up the dark for a moment. He mentions his own unexplainable experiences with tzaddikim, which he will not tell in public, and introduces the mussar chaburah in Williamsburg and the respected Yid who taught it.

title.en: The Slonimer Rebbe and the borrowed dishes

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells a story witnessed by his mentor: when the Slonimer Rebbe visited Yerushalayim, he came to eat at the home of a poor, beardless chassid and would not eat, sensing that the dishes lent by a bearded neighbor had not been toveled. The Rebbe told the chassid that in Heaven they would ask him where his beard is, but of the neighbor they would ask where the Yid is.

title.en: The untoveled knife and the questionable chicken

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells what Mr. Singer told him: a Rebbe's gabbai, a guest in his father's house, refused to cut the challah with a new knife that the boy had falsely claimed to have toveled. He then tells how the Rav of Brisk, given a chicken for the road by Rabbi Binyamin Diskin that turned out to be questionable, did not eat it.

title.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov's pancake; believing beyond seeing

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Yeshuos Yaakov avoided a butter pancake made in a meat pan, explaining it was no wonder but that the pancake had splashed him in the face. He concludes that such glimpses are rare lightning flashes in a deep hester panim, brings the machlokes of the Apta Rav and the Kotzker Rebbe over seeing or believing the ushpizin, and says our mission is to believe in Hashem despite His disguise.

catalogTitle: תפילה בידידות ובאחדות (ניגון)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches bachurim that davening together, with love between friends, strengthens the tefillah, and that coming on time to davening and learning is no small matter, as the closed window of the mishmar of Bilgah and a story of the Chiddushei HaRim show.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with beginning davening together: Pesukei d'Zimra opens with words all say together, the Shirah at the sea was said together, and the angels praise Hashem 'together'. Like roped mountain climbers, one who slips is held by the others. Togetherness rests on love: the angels speak together because 'all are beloved'. He brings the Radbaz, who let a son daven with his friends against his mother's wish, and the friendship the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Arizal built among their disciples. Davening and learning carry each other, so a bachur cannot learn well without davening well. Turning to coming on time, he brings the window of the mishmar of Bilgah, closed by one opinion for coming late, as a closed window of heavenly blessing. A soul that came too late to the Chiddushei HaRim lost its tikkun, measure for measure. One must correct oneself before Moshiach comes.

en: Beginning davening together is a great matter: the Shirah at the sea and the praise of the angels were said together, and those who daven together hold each other up like roped climbers.
Davening together rests on love between friends; the angels say their praise together because they all love one another.
Davening well and learning well depend on each other like two feet; a bachur whose main task is learning still cannot learn well without davening well.
Coming late is no small thing: by one opinion in the Gemara the mishmar of Bilgah had its window closed for generations because it once came late.
A soul that came too late to the Chiddushei HaRim lost its tikkun, measure for measure for having come late to davening and learning in its lifetime.
One must correct oneself before Moshiach comes, because when he comes it will already be too late.

title.en: Beginning davening together

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows from the opening of Pesukei d'Zimra in both nuschaos, from the Shirah at the sea and from the angels' praise 'together' that davening together is a great matter. He compares those davening together to mountain climbers roped to one another.

title.en: Love between friends makes the davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a special angel tries to keep people from coming on time to begin together, and explains that togetherness rests on love, as with the angels who are 'all beloved' and the singers at the sea. He brings the Radbaz on davening with friends against a mother's wish, and the love the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Arizal fostered among their disciples.

title.en: Davening and learning carry each other

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that good davening brings good learning and the reverse, like two feet, and that only Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his companions could learn without stopping to daven. He brings the Chasam Sofer's answer about his long Shemoneh Esrei and explains why he stresses davening to yeshivah bachurim.

title.en: The closed window of Bilgah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara at the end of Sukkah about Miriam bas Bilgah and the window of the mishmar of Bilgah that was closed, and the other opinion that it was closed because the mishmar once came late. He explains the 24 windows as rooted in heavenly windows of blessing, so that coming late closes a person's flow of blessing, and adds that coming late on the first day of the Beis HaMikdash led to its destruction.

title.en: The soul that came too late

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells, from a reliable sefer of stories of tzaddikim, how the Chiddushei HaRim, who worked to bring tikkun to souls, told one soul on his last erev Shabbos that it had come too late, and asks why the soul came late.

title.en: Measure for measure; come on time

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that the soul came late measure for measure, for coming late to davening and learning in its lifetime, and calls coming late the work of a great yetzer hara. Especially now, with the world in turmoil, one must correct oneself before Moshiach comes, for then it will be too late; he then leads last week's niggun.

catalogTitle: סיפורי מעשיות מהמגיד הגדול ממזריטש זצוק"ל

oneLiner.en: For the yahrzeit of the Maggid of Mezritch, the Mashgiach tells how the Maggid repaired a dream-sin through Tehillim before coming to the Ba'al Shem Tov, and how his holy vision saved a town from a cruel poretz.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the yahrzeit of the Maggid of Mezritch, successor of the Ba'al Shem Tov and Rebbe of the great tzaddikim of his generation. He tells how the Maggid dreamt on Tisha B'Av that he made a blessing on an apple, and woke in fear of the wasted blessing. Saying Tehillim with tears, he dozed and saw a garden of trees whose fruit, leaves, branches and finally trunks fell away with each book. From this the Mashgiach explains that every deed plants in heaven, that chiddushei Torah create new heavens which can annul a decree, as the Arizal's Shabbos zemer says. The Maggid then came to the Besht, who taught him to uproot a sin from its root. A second story shows how the Maggid delayed a messenger so that he met the official over all poritzim. The Mashgiach closes that all Chassidus flows from the Besht through the Maggid, and urges strengthening before Moshiach.

en: Every deed a person does plants something in heaven: a mitzvah grows plantings of holiness, a sin plants for the sitra achra.
The greater the person, the greater the damage of his sins and the greater the repair of his mitzvos.
Chiddushei Torah create new heavens, and in a new heaven a decree does not yet exist, so it can be annulled.
The Ba'al Shem Tov taught the Maggid that a sin must be uprooted from its root, not only its branches.
The Maggid's holy, open eyes saw that the messenger had to be held back to meet the chief official on exactly the right day.
The Maggid's true greatness was not his wonders but spreading the Besht's avodas Hashem, so that all are his students.

candidateTopics: the Ba'al Shem Tov and his students

title.en: The Maggid's Tisha B'Av dream

summary.en: For the Maggid's yahrzeit the Mashgiach begins the story of how he came to the Ba'al Shem Tov: he dreamt on Tisha B'Av that he made a blessing on an apple, and after weeping Tehillim he saw a garden whose fruit fell. The Mashgiach explains that every deed plants in heaven, for holiness or for the sitra achra.

title.en: Chiddushei Torah create new heavens

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that a person's Torah chiddushim create new heavens, which can annul a decree, and shows it in the Arizal's Shabbos morning zemer: chiddushim at the Shabbos table make a new heaven with its own sun.

title.en: Five books of Tehillim and the root

summary.en: With each book of Tehillim the Maggid saw more of the garden fall, until with the fifth nothing was left. He then came to the Ba'al Shem Tov, who taught him to uproot a sin from its root.

title.en: The messenger to Petersburg

summary.en: A town suffering under a cruel poretz sends a messenger to Petersburg on the Maggid's advice; the Maggid holds him back for two days, then rushes him off, and on the way he meets the chief official over all poritzim on the Czar's birthday, who replaces the poretz.

title.en: All are students of the Maggid

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the Maggid's greatness was spreading the Besht's avodas Hashem, from which all later Jewish holiness flows, mentions the yahrzeit of R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh, and closes with lechayim and a call to strengthen in Torah, tefillah and chesed in times of the footsteps of Moshiach.

catalogTitle: אגרת התניא אודות תפילה; מלוה מלכה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach learns the Ba'al HaTanya's letter protesting against those who push away a long davener, tells a true story of a dybbuk driven out by the Shinava Rav, and explains why Yehuda was sent ahead to Goshen and how the Melave Malka inaugurates the new week.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a letter of the Ba'al HaTanya in Iggeres HaKodesh, written when he heard that people would not let a man who davens at length lead the prayers. Chazal say that prolonging one's tefillah prolongs life, so the Mashgiach calls the claim of having no time a false calculation. The letter explains that in earlier generations Torah was the main avodah, but in the time before Moshiach it is tefillah, which needs contemplation of each word, and it asks for orderly, unhurried davening together. The Mashgiach then sets out the two conditions of a proper story, a known source and a lesson, and tells, through Rabbi Elazar Brizel, how the Shinava Rav freed a girl from a dybbuk, linking it to the Chofetz Chaim's words about our test of emunah. Finally he explains that Yehuda, the root of hodaah, inaugurated Goshen, just as the Melave Malka of Dovid HaMelech inaugurates the week.

en: The Ba'al HaTanya was deeply pained to hear that a man who davens at length was kept from leading the prayers, since Chazal say that prolonging tefillah prolongs life.
In earlier generations Torah was the main avodah; in the time before Moshiach the main avodah is tefillah.
Davening means contemplating each word, which can only be done slowly, so as to awaken the hidden love in every Jew's heart before Shema.
A story worth telling needs two things: a known source, so one knows it is true, and a lesson one can take away.
The Chofetz Chaim said there would be no more dybbukim, since the test of the last generation before Moshiach is to believe without seeing.
Yehuda, named for thanking Hashem, was sent to inaugurate Goshen, and the Melave Malka, the seudah of Dovid HaMelech, likewise inaugurates the new week with songs of praise.

candidateTopics: tefillah as the avodah of ikvesa dimeshicha

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya's letter on long davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach introduces the Iggeres HaKodesh, letters the Ba'al HaTanya sent his chassidim, and reads one written when he heard that a man who davens at length was kept from leading the prayers. He explains the letter's argument from Chazal that prolonging tefillah prolongs life, calls the claim of 'no time' a false calculation, and explains how the chazan's repetition covers one who must leave.

title.en: Tefillah as the avodah before Moshiach

summary.en: Answering the complaint that the chassidim invented a new stringency, the letter explains that the early generations served mainly through Torah while in the time before Moshiach the main avodah is tefillah, requiring slow contemplation in Pesukei DeZimra and the blessings of Shema. The Mashgiach adds that the early great souls could daven briefly because their minds were open and unclouded by sin, and he reads the letter's request for orderly davening together and its rules for choosing chazanim.

title.en: What makes a true story; dybbukim and emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets out two conditions for telling a story, a known source and a lesson, and presents the source of his story, Rabbi Elazar Brizel, who heard it from his father. He describes what was once seen of sinful souls fleeing the angels of destruction into a living person as a dybbuk, and brings the Chofetz Chaim's statement that there would be no more dybbukim because our generation's test is emunah amid hiddenness.

title.en: The Shinava Rav and the dybbuk

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how a girl possessed by a dybbuk was brought to the Shinava Rav's shalosh seudos, where the dybbuk cried out at his holy words, and after Havdalah the gabbai was sent to a certain grave and the girl was healed. He then applies it: many of us carry inner 'dybbukim', forces born of sins that keep us from learning and davening properly, which must be uprooted before Moshiach comes.

title.en: Yehuda sent to Goshen and the Melave Malka

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Yaakov sent Yehuda, and not Yissachar or Levi, ahead to Goshen, and explains it through the custom of chanukas habayis: a place is inaugurated with praise of Hashem, and Yehuda is the root of hodaah and of Dovid HaMelech. So too the Melave Malka, the seudah of Dovid HaMelech, inaugurates the coming week, and he closes with blessings that the coming days of darkness in Teves turn to joy.

catalogTitle: The Multitudes at הר סיני - An Iron Proof of the Truth of the תורה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the emunah of Klal Yisrael rests not on the word of one man but on what millions of people saw together at Har Sinai and in the Midbar, a testimony that could never have been fabricated.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with emunas tzaddikim, belief in tzaddikim alongside belief in Hashem, and says tzaddikim know everything because everything is in the Torah. He illustrates this with the story of the Ramban and his student Avner, who found his name hinted in a passuk of Haazinu, and with the Chazon Ish, who guided surgeons from his knowledge of Hilchos Treifos. The Torah is the blueprint of the world, and it also foretells the future: the division of Eretz Yisrael, the promise that nobody will covet a man's land when he goes up to Yerushalayim, galus, and the survival of the Jewish people and of the Torah while the empires that oppressed them vanished. After a question on Rashi's first comment, he turns to his main theme. Christianity and Islam each began with one man whom people believed. Jewish emunah rests on millions who stood at Har Sinai and lived through forty years of open miracles, recorded in a Torah that every Jew received and that was copied identically across the world.

en: Emunah includes emunas tzaddikim: believing in Moshe Rabbeinu and the tzaddikim, not only in Hashem.
Everything in the world is in the Torah, because Hashem looked into the Torah and created the world; this is how tzaddikim know everything.
The Torah foretells the future, from the division of Eretz Yisrael to galus and the eternal survival of the Jewish people and the Torah.
An event witnessed by a multitude, such as the existence of a president or of Alexander the Great, cannot be fabricated or denied.
Christianity and Islam rest on the word of one person; Jewish emunah rests on the experience of millions at Har Sinai.
The Torah, written at the end of forty years in the Midbar, recorded what the whole people had experienced and was copied letter for letter by every Jew down the generations.

candidateTopics: proof of the truth of the Torah
everything is contained in the Torah
Judaism compared with Christianity and Islam

title.en: Emunas tzaddikim

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with emunas tzaddikim: at Kriyas Yam Suf the Jews believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant. He says he has himself seen the ruach hakodesh of tzaddikim, and that tzaddikim know everything because everything is in the Torah.

title.en: The Ramban and Avner in Haazinu

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the story of the Ramban's student Avner, who went off the derech, challenged the Ramban's teaching that Haazinu contains every Jew's history, and was shown his name in the third letters of a passuk. Shaken, Avner did teshuvah and set off in a boat without oars.

title.en: Everything is in the Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Chazon Ish showed surgeons how to perform brain surgery, saying he knew it from Hilchos Treifos. He brings the Ramban that Shlomo HaMelech knew everything from the Torah, explains that the Torah is the blueprint of creation, and notes that the Zohar says the world is round. He adds that, unlike other religions' books, the Torah foretells the future, and it was given identically to all of Klal Yisrael.

title.en: The Torah's promises come true

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows the Torah foretelling the future: the nachalos of the shevatim and Yehoshua's conquest; the promise that nobody will covet a man's land when he goes up to Yerushalayim three times a year; galus and the survival of the Jews while Bavel, Paras, Yavan and Rome disappeared; and that the Torah will not be forgotten, as seen in the growth of Torah learning after the war.

title.en: A question on the first Rashi

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi's first comment on Bereishis, that the Torah should have begun with the mitzvah of Rosh Chodesh, the first mitzvah given to Yisrael, and asks how it can be called the first when milah, and according to one opinion gid hanasheh, were commanded earlier.

title.en: What a multitude witnessed cannot be denied

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets out why we believe: of the three main religions, Christianity and Islam accept the Torah but claim Hashem changed His mind. He then builds the principle that an event witnessed by hundreds of thousands cannot be fabricated, using President Ford, George Washington, Julius Caesar and Alexander the Great, whom the Gemara mentions meeting Shimon HaTzaddik.

title.en: Religions built on one man

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Christianity began with one charismatic man whose teaching, built on Judaism, people believed, and how Islam began with Mohammed, whom the Rambam calls a madman, whose book contradicts recorded history. In both cases people believed one person.

title.en: Millions at Har Sinai

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that Jews do not believe because Moshe said so, but because a few million people stood at Har Sinai and heard Hashem. The Torah, written at the end of forty years, recorded the miracles they all lived through, every Jew was commanded to have a Sefer Torah, and the Torah was copied letter for letter so that Jews cut off from each other for centuries hold the identical text.

catalogTitle: מתינות' טהרה' לזכור את ה'' ועוד דברי הלכה והשקפה בתפילה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches a series of practices for avodas Hashem: davening without haste, purity in the mikveh, brachos and amen, the hazmanah of leshem yichud, tefillah b'tzibbur and binding oneself to Klal Yisrael, and closes with two stories of Rabbi Moshe of Lelov.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a letter of the Ba'al HaTanya about ba'alei tefillah: one who has business and will rush should not go to the amud, weekday Shacharis should take at least an hour and a half, and on Shabbos busy people must daven at greater length. He turns to purity in the mikveh, how to conduct oneself there, and the advice to immerse with the intention of receiving the kedushah of Moshiach. He then speaks about brachos, which bring shefa to the world and are completed by amen, and about leshem yichud as hazmanah, preparation that brings kedushah to every mitzvah. He discusses starting Baruch She'amar with the tzibbur, and explains that saying a mitzvah is done in the name of all Israel protects it from any accuser. He closes with the yahrzeit of Rabbi Moshe of Lelov, his attempt to reach the Kosel and bring the geulah, and a story of a chassid saved by the Rebbe's glass.

en: Following the Ba'al HaTanya, one who will rush should not go to the amud, and weekday Shacharis should take at least an hour and a half.
In the mikveh one should guard one's eyes, go in and out quickly, and not talk, because it has its own kedushah.
A brachah draws shefa onto the whole world, and it is completed only when someone answers amen.
Leshem yichud is a hazmanah, a preparation, and preparing for a mitzvah brings kedushah to the person and to the object of the mitzvah.
One who davens at length in a fast minyan should begin Baruch She'amar with the congregation, and this counts as tefillah b'tzibbur.
Doing a mitzvah in the name of all Israel binds a person to Klal Yisrael, on whom no accuser can find a blemish.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya on davening without haste

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads from a letter of the Ba'al HaTanya about ba'alei tefillah: a busy person who will rush should not go to the amud, weekday Shacharis should last at least an hour and a half, and on Shabbos those who lack time during the week must daven longer.

title.en: Purity in the mikveh and hoping for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks about the customs of going to the mikveh and how to behave there: guarding the eyes, going in and out quickly, and not talking. He then says one must hope for Moshiach every day and advises immersing with the intention of preparing to receive the kedushah of Moshiach.

title.en: Brachos, amen and leshem yichud

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a brachah draws shefa onto the world, that one must remember the Ribono shel Olam when saying it, and that amen completes it. He then explains leshem yichud as a hazmanah that brings kedushah into every mitzvah, using the examples of writing tefillin and tying tzitzis.

title.en: Starting Baruch She'amar with the tzibbur

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that one who davens at length should begin Baruch She'amar together with the congregation, which counts as tefillah b'tzibbur. He mentions that chassidim follow the Shulchan Aruch of the Ba'al HaTanya, written at the Maggid's request, discusses where it differs from the Mishnah Berurah, and adds that saying Tehillim together after davening also belongs to the tefillah b'tzibbur.

title.en: In the name of all Israel

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that leshem yichud ends with the words 'in the name of all Israel', and that before davening one should accept the mitzvah of loving a fellow Jew. A mitzvah of a private person can be lost to accusers, but one done in the name of all Israel cannot be harmed, and he calls this an insurance policy for every mitzvah.

title.en: Rabbi Moshe of Lelov and the Kosel

summary.en: For the yahrzeit of Rabbi Moshe of Lelov, the Mashgiach tells how he travelled to Eretz Yisrael to bring the geulah by reaching the Kosel, lost the Lubliner kiddush cup on the way, fell ill in Yerushalayim, was turned back by stone-throwing Arabs and passed away. He adds that one must daven for the great yeshuah for Klal Yisrael without harm to any Jew.

title.en: The chassid, the robber and the Rebbe's glass

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a chassid of Rabbi Moshe of Lelov who needed a yeshuah in parnasah and received a glass from the Rebbe as a segulah for parnasah and protection. When a robber in a forest took his borrowed money, the glass became the means of his rescue and of a large reward, and the Mashgiach closes with a blessing.

catalogTitle: דיבורים המעוררים על ענין קבלת עול מלכות שמים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that through Kerias Shema a Jew draws the acceptance of Hashem's kingship onto his own limbs and onto the whole creation, and urges the bachurim to learn before davening and to find their own shlichus where it is hardest.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the several Kerias Shemas said each day and explains that the rabbinic ones are needed for the soul: a mitzvah d'Rabbanan reaches even higher than one from the Torah, since obeying the Sages is Hashem's own command, and its leniency in doubt comes only from the Sages' own will. Kerias Shema draws kabbalas ol malchus Shamayim onto all 248 limbs, and since the world too has 248 limbs, a Jew's Shema in New York can give a Jew in Africa yiras Shamayim in his test. Rosh Hashanah is the Kerias Shema of the year, leading to the end of days, when all nations will come to Yerushalayim. With the parable of a main power switch he shows how great a Jew's every act is. He then urges learning before davening, especially on Shabbos, noting how fiercely the yetzer hara fights it, and teaches that each Jew belongs to a limb of Adam Harishon with his own shlichus, recognized by desire and by difficulty.

en: Through Kerias Shema a Jew draws kabbalas ol malchus Shamayim onto all his limbs.
A mitzvah d'Rabbanan reaches higher than a mitzvah d'Oraisa, because the Torah itself commands obeying the Sages.
Since the world also has 248 limbs, one Jew's Kerias Shema draws yiras Shamayim onto the whole creation, even onto a Jew far away.
Learning before davening is a great matter, and the yetzer hara's fierce opposition to it is itself the proof of its importance.
Every Jew belongs to a limb of Adam Harishon and has his own shlichus in the world.
A person recognizes his shlichus by two signs: a strong desire for a mitzvah, and great difficulty in doing it.

candidateTopics: 248 limbs of man and the world
signs of the generation of Moshiach

title.en: Kerias Shema and the power of a mitzvah d'Rabbanan

summary.en: The Mashgiach lists the Kerias Shemas said each day and explains that each one draws kabbalas ol malchus Shamayim onto all the limbs. He urges saying the whole Shema before davening, especially on Shabbos, and explains why a mitzvah d'Rabbanan reaches higher than one d'Oraisa, why it is still lenient in doubt, and how Kerias Shema al hamitah destroys the harmful forces created by sins.

title.en: Kabbalas ol on the limbs of the whole world

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that just as a person has 248 limbs, so does the world, and a Jew who says Shema with great kavanah in New York can bring sudden yiras Shamayim to a Jew in Africa facing a test. Even washing negel vasser weakens the ruach hatumah everywhere, and a Jew's Shema reaches even the nations.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah, the end of days and Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Rosh Hashanah the Kerias Shema of the year, when one asks that the kabbalas ol of the day spread over the whole world, and describes the end of days when all nations will come to Yerushalayim and the enemies of Israel will be revived for judgment. He digresses on Saddam Hussein, who saw himself as Nebuchadnezzar and used the Jewish calendar like Haman, and on Pharaoh, who knew every Divine name but Hashem's, concluding that the signs show this is the generation of Moshiach.

title.en: The main switch: how great a Jew is

summary.en: Returning to Kerias Shema, the Mashgiach says it draws kabbalas ol onto the whole creation, even the animals and the angels, and that a Jew must know how great he is. He compares each limb to the main switch at the power company that lights all of New York: a mitzvah brings light to the highest worlds, while a sin is like a bomb. He then begins to stress learning before davening, citing Rabbi Aharon of Karlin.

title.en: Learning before davening and the yetzer hara

summary.en: The Mashgiach admits learning before davening is hard on weekdays for those who learn late at night, but says it must be done on Shabbos. He tells how he urged the people of his beis medrash, fine and obedient Jews, to come learn before davening, yet few come; the yetzer hara lets a person eat kugel or make kiddush but blocks learning before davening, which shows how important it is.

title.en: Each Jew a limb of Adam Harishon

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Jewish souls hung on all the limbs of Adam Harishon, so each Jew comes into the world for a particular shlichus. Tzaddik or rasha is a person's own choice, but even tzaddikim differ: one from the head longs to learn, like Moshe Rabbeinu; one from the throat pours out his heart in tefillah, like Dovid Hamelech; one from the feet goes around collecting tzedakah. The stages of a life, too, correspond to the limbs.

title.en: Where it is hard, there lies the shlichus

summary.en: The Mashgiach gives two signs of a person's shlichus: a strong desire for a mitzvah, and difficulty, since the yetzer hara fights hardest where it matters. He supports this from the Mishnah's miracle that the Kohen Gadol never became tamei on Yom Kippur, explained by the Tosafos Yom Tov, and tells the bachurim that whatever is hard for them, such as learning before davening, is their shlichus, and that now their whole task is Torah.

catalogTitle: הכנה לתפילה; חשיבות אמירת קטרת; ניסים בGulf War

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches how to prepare for davening and why saying the ketores matters so much, and sees in the missiles that harmed no one during the Gulf War open miracles, which only one who does not want to believe can deny.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach lists ways to prepare for davening: giving tzedakah first, because a person's money is part of his nefesh and tzedakah clears away the accusers who block a mitzvah from rising; binding oneself to the tzaddikim and to the tzaddik of the generation, and accepting the mitzvah of loving one's fellow Jew; and being among the first ten in shul. He then stresses saying the ketores with the tzibbur and knowing what it means, since it drives away harmful forces, and brings the Stoliner Rebbe's assurance that it protects from illness. Turning to the Iraqi missiles that had just fallen on Eretz Yisroel without killing anyone, he calls them open miracles. Through Moshe's 'kachatzos', a story from Telz and the Sfas Emes on Pharaoh, he explains that a person who denies such wonders does not want to believe. He closes that everyone must daven and learn as Hashem's soldiers, with the ketores as their missile.

en: The Mashgiach says one should give tzedakah before davening and before every mitzvah, since it removes the accusers who stop a mitzvah from reaching the Kisei HaKavod.

Before davening one should bind oneself to the tzaddikim and the tzaddik of the generation, and accept upon oneself the mitzvah of loving one's fellow Jew, which includes all the mitzvos as that tzaddik includes all the souls.
The Mashgiach stresses the great value of being among the first ten in shul, with whom the Shechinah speaks in the morning.
Saying the ketores together with the tzibbur, and knowing what one is saying, counts as offering it and drives away harmful forces.
The Mashgiach sees the missiles that fell on Eretz Yisroel without killing anyone as open miracles, which only a person who does not want to believe can deny.
Everyone must be a soldier of Hashem: learning, davening and saying the ketores are the Jews' real strength in the war.

title.en: Tzedakah before davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that one gives tzedakah before davening, explains that money is part of a person's nefesh and that tzedakah clears away the accusers who block a mitzvah, and mentions the custom of giving at Vayevarech David.

title.en: Bond with the tzaddik; the first ten

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains binding oneself before davening to the tzaddikim, to the tzaddik of the generation and to all of Klal Yisroel through accepting 'v'ahavta l'reiacha kamocha', and then the great value of being among the first ten in shul.

title.en: Saying the ketores and knowing its meaning

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the ketores stopped the plague and drives away harmful forces, that learning its parsha counts as offering it, and that this requires understanding the words, as with Torah she'b'al peh.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe and the Gulf War missiles

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Stoliner Rebbe's words that saying ketores with a minyan protects from illness, then speaks of the Iraqi missiles fired at Eretz Yisroel in the last two days that killed no one, and calls it an open miracle that happens again and again.

title.en: Not wanting to believe: 'kachatzos' and the Telz ceiling

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara on why Moshe said 'kachatzos', explains that a person who does not want to believe will call even proven wonders a lie, and tells R' Yosef Bloch's story of the ceiling in a Telz club that stopped falling once a dead man's blood was buried.

title.en: Pharaoh's refusal and the tzaddikim's assurance

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Sfas Emes that Pharaoh did not even want to want to submit, then recalls how in Hitler's time the tzaddikim davened on Har HaZeisim and assured that the enemy would not enter Eretz Yisroel, and Rommel turned back at Alexandria.

title.en: Soldiers of Hashem: a thousand for each tribe twice

summary.en: The Mashgiach says one must still daven, brings the Midrash that 'a thousand for each tribe' is said twice because a thousand went to war and a thousand sat and learned, and concludes that learning, davening and saying the ketores are the Jews' missiles in this war.

catalogTitle: “משה אב לנביאים” - the Root of the Yiddishe Mesorah

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains, from the Rambam, that our emunah in the Torah rests not on Moshe Rabbeinu's miracles but on the whole nation hearing Hashem appoint him at Har Sinai, so that every mitzvah and every other navi is believed only through Moshe Rabbeinu.

abstract.en: Continuing from last week, the Mashgiach reads the Rambam in Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah chapter 8: Klal Yisroel did not believe in Moshe Rabbeinu because of his signs, since a sign can always leave a doubt that it was a trick; the signs in the midbar were done because they were needed. They believed because at Har Sinai every Jew was a navi and heard Hashem speak to Moshe and appoint him. Therefore a navi who performs wonders to contradict Moshe is not heard, like witnesses who claim it is night when the beis din sees it is day. Listening to any other navi is a mitzvah, like listening to two witnesses, and not proof. The Mashgiach reads a letter in the Igros Moshe on why a tradition seen by a multitude cannot be false. He closes by answering Rashi's question on the first mitzvah, and explains the Ani Maamin that Moshe is the father of all the nevi'im.

en: According to the Rambam, Klal Yisroel's belief in Moshe Rabbeinu was not based on his signs, because a sign always leaves a small doubt that it was a trick.
At Har Sinai every Jew was a navi and heard Hashem speak to Moshe and appoint him to give the rest of the Torah; this is the basis of believing in him.
A navi who shows wonders in order to contradict Moshe Rabbeinu's nevuah is not listened to, just as two witnesses who say it is night are not believed when the beis din sees it is day.
Listening to any other navi is a mitzvah under the Torah's conditions, like listening to witnesses, not a certainty; only Moshe Rabbeinu's nevuah is beyond doubt.
A tradition that a multitude saw with their own eyes cannot be false, since a lie about something that hundreds of thousands witnessed would be exposed at once.
Every mitzvah, even milah, and every navi before or after Moshe is accepted only because Moshe Rabbeinu transmitted it, which is why he is called the father of all the nevi'im.

title.en: Not belief through signs

summary.en: The Mashgiach recalls that our emunah rests on a mesorah the whole nation saw, and reads the Rambam in Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah chapter 8 that Klal Yisroel did not believe in Moshe Rabbeinu because of his signs. He compares a sign to a magician's trick that still leaves a doubt, and explains that the signs in the midbar were done because they were needed.

title.en: All Yidden were nevi'im at Sinai

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at Matan Torah every Jew was a navi and heard Hashem speak to Moshe and appoint him, as the pesukim in Shemos promise. Therefore a navi who performs wonders to refute Moshe Rabbeinu is not heard, like witnesses who say it is night while the beis din sees it is day.

title.en: Listening to a navi is like listening to witnesses

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a navi may command a temporary deviation, as Eliyahu offered korbanos on Har Hakarmel, but never avodah zarah. Listening to such a navi is a mitzvah like accepting two witnesses, which is not foolproof, as the case of Navos shows; only Moshe Rabbeinu's nevuah, which the whole nation saw and heard, is certain.

title.en: A letter on proving the Torah true

summary.en: The Mashgiach sums up the Rambam and reads a letter from the Igros Moshe to someone troubled by doubts about the truth of the Torah. The answer is not philosophy but the mesorah of a multitude: a father cannot tell his son he saw something together with 600,000 people if nobody else saw it, and even the nations accept the miracles of Mitzrayim and the midbar.

title.en: The first mitzvah and Moshe av lanevi'im

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to Rashi's question why the Torah did not begin with HaChodesh hazeh lachem, the first mitzvah, though milah and gid hanasheh came earlier. He answers that those mitzvos are known only because Moshe told us about them, so HaChodesh hazeh is the first mitzvah heard from Moshe, and explains the Ani Maamin that Moshe is the father of all nevi'im before and after him.

catalogTitle: תלמוד תורה עם יראת שמים מבטלין אויבינו

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches the bachurim that Torah learning is Klal Yisroel's real weapon, as Chizkiyahu understood against Sancheiriv, so leaving the beis medrash is like deserting the army, and Adar is the time of war against Amalek, the yetzer hara.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens in Adar by telling the bachurim that learning is hard, yet Klal Yisroel now needs great zechusim. He brings the Gemara that Chizkiyahu planted a sword at the beis medrash for anyone who would not learn, and notes that a person may engage in earning a living. Why then the sword? Because it was wartime with Sancheiriv, and the halacha is that a soldier who flees is cut down; Chizkiyahu knew that Israel's war is fought with Torah, and the Gemara says Sancheiriv's yoke was broken by the oil burned in the batei medrash. So the war is in the beis medrash: one must learn with strength, a niggun, warmth and love for the Torah, never with lightheadedness. Adar is a war against Amalek, which after Purim is called chametz, the yetzer hara. Amalek has a body and a soul; the soul is the yetzer hara. Those who fight well receive heavenly decorations and rise in madreigos.

en: Chizkiyahu forced learning with a sword because Torah was Israel's weapon in the war with Sancheiriv, and leaving the beis medrash was like deserting.
The Mashgiach says the real front is in the beis medrash, and Klal Yisroel now needs great zechusim from the bachurim's learning.
Learning must be done with strength, a niggun, warmth and love of Torah, as hearing what Hashem says, never lightheadedly or lounging.
Adar, until Erev Pesach, is a time of war against Amalek, who after Purim is called chametz, both meaning the yetzer hara.
Learning, davening and guarding oneself from bad thoughts and from looking where one should not are all the war against Amalek, rewarded with heavenly decorations and higher madreigos.

title.en: Chizkiyahu's sword at the beis medrash

summary.en: In Adar the Mashgiach tells the bachurim that learning is hard but Klal Yisroel needs zechusim now. He brings the Gemara that in Chizkiyahu's time everyone was learned and a sword stood at the beis medrash against those who would not learn, and adds that one may engage in earning a living, as the Shulchan Aruch HaRav says.

title.en: The war against Sancheiriv was fought with Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why a sword was needed and answers that it was wartime, when Sancheiriv was approaching Yerushalayim. He brings the halacha that a soldier who flees is struck down, and the Gemara that Sancheiriv's yoke was broken by the oil burned in the batei medrash, so sitting out of the beis medrash was desertion.

title.en: How to learn: with fire and love of Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies this to the present: Jews need great zechusim, so one must learn with strength, a niggun and interest, as hearing what Hashem says. He warns that learning with lightheadedness or lounging is not Torah, speaks of kissing a fallen sefer, and explains that Gemara is like burning coals, to be learned with warmth and fire.

title.en: Adar: war against Amalek and chametz

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that all of Adar, with its parshiyos and Purim, is a war against Amalek, who after Purim is called chametz; both are the yetzer hara in the world and in oneself, which is why chametz is treated so strictly, as the Radbaz explains. The war is fought with Torah and the mitzvos of the time, and with simcha in being a Jew.

title.en: Amalek's body and soul; heavenly decorations

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the two pesukim about erasing Amalek: Amalek, like a person, has a body and a soul; the body is killed physically, and the soul, the yetzer hara, is nullified. He compares those who daven and learn well to soldiers who receive decorations and promotions, which in avodas Hashem are the madreigos up to ruach hakodesh.

title.en: Sent to the front: the bachurim's war

summary.en: Like soldiers addressed before being sent to the front, the Mashgiach tells the bachurim that Adar sends them to war against a merciless enemy, and that all of Klal Yisroel relies on their learning, davening and guarding themselves. He closes with a brachah that they be decorated, defeat Amalek and merit the world of Moshiach and the Beis HaMikdash.

catalogTitle: אהבת ישראל; עולמות של תפילהGulf War ;

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that through ahavas Yisroel a Jew joins the whole of Klal Yisroel and so completes all the mitzvos, and that the same bond carries his davening up through the worlds, leading to a call to daven in the days of mercy, also for the soldiers fighting in the Gulf War.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rashi's words that ahavas Yisroel is a great principle of the Torah, and explains through the Arizal, brought by the Bnei Yissaschar, that every Jew must fulfil all 613 mitzvos, which correspond to the limbs and give them life at techiyas hameisim. Mitzvos a person cannot do himself he completes through learning their laws and through ahavas Yisroel, which makes him a partner of every other Jew. He then turns to judging others favorably, following Rabbeinu Yonah, and shows from Dovid and Nasan that a person who judges another judges himself. Love of Hashem is measured by love of Jews, so one must share Klal Yisroel's pain. Before davening one accepts ahavas Yisroel, and davening climbs through the worlds with each kaddish as a staircase; one who comes late loses it. Tefillah is dveikus with the heart. The Mashgiach urges davening in these days of mercy, also for the American soldiers, and tells an Apter Rav prophecy of a war that is good for the Jews.

en: Every Jew must fulfil all the mitzvos, and through ahavas Yisroel he becomes a partner in the mitzvos other Jews do, completing what he himself cannot.
Whoever judges another person is in effect judging himself, so one must judge every Jew favorably.
How much a person loves Hashem can be measured by how much he loves a Jew.
Davening rises from world to world, and each kaddish is the staircase that lifts the davener to the next world; one who comes late misses it.
Tefillah means cleaving to Hashem, and it must be with the heart and with a feeling of pleasure, not only the words.
The months from Adar to Sivan are days of mercy when the gates of tefillah are open, and they should be used to daven for Klal Yisroel and also for the soldiers fighting for the Jews.

title.en: Ahavas Yisroel completes all the mitzvos

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls ahavas Yisroel a great principle of the Torah and brings the Arizal, via the Bnei Yissaschar, that every Jew must keep all the mitzvos, which give life to the limbs at techiyas hameisim. A mitzvah one cannot do, like pidyon haben, is completed by learning its laws and by ahavas Yisroel, which makes one a partner of the Jew who does it.

title.en: Judging favorably, and judging oneself

summary.en: The Mashgiach lays out, following Rabbeinu Yonah, how far one must judge a tzaddik, an average person and a rasha favorably, with the Gemara's story of the worker who judged his employer favorably. He then shows from Nasan's parable to Dovid that a person who passes judgment on another is passing judgment on himself.

title.en: Love of Hashem measured by love of Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows from the order of davening that love of Hashem follows Hashem's love for Yisroel, and brings from tzaddikim that love of Hashem is measured by love of a Jew. Ahavas Yisroel means sharing the pain of Jews, including those in Eretz Yisroel in the war, and accepting ahavas Yisroel before davening opens the gates of tefillah.

title.en: The worlds of davening and the kaddish staircase

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that davening climbs from Asiyah to Yetzirah, Beriah and Atzilus, and that each kaddish is a staircase to the next world, with a kaddish on the way down after Shemoneh Esrei. One who comes late has missed the staircase; he can still say the words, but rising without it takes enormous kavanah.

title.en: Tefillah as dveikus, and davening for the soldiers

summary.en: The Mashgiach defines tefillah as cleaving to Hashem, which must be felt as pleasure and done with the whole heart. He urges using the merciful months from Adar to Sivan to daven for Klal Yisroel and for the American soldiers, since there is an obligation to pray for the peace of one's country and these soldiers are fighting the wicked man of Iraq who threatens Eretz Yisroel.

title.en: Which stories of tzaddikim can be trusted

summary.en: Before telling a story of the Apter Rav, the Mashgiach warns that most story books are false or mixed with falsehood, and that a story of tzaddikim, which is like Torah, must come from a trustworthy source. He presents the recorded stories of Reb Motel Slonimer, who accepted stories only from reliable people and whose chassid wrote them down the same day.

title.en: The Apter Rav's war that is good for the Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells, through Reb Motel Slonimer, the Apter Rav's words that before Moshiach the nations will be dragged into a war that is good for the Jews, and explains that the present war is the first such war, since the enemy wants to destroy Eretz Yisroel. He concludes that one must daven for the soldiers, describes the chapter of Tehillim said for them in his beis medrash, and urges using these days of mercy.

catalogTitle: התעוררות לתפילה ולעבודת ה'

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach rouses bachurim to long, heartfelt davening, explaining that every word of tefillah is a heichal of Gan Eden and that every day and every person has a mission that will not come again.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Alter Rebbe's first letter in Iggeres HaKodesh: those who have time, such as melamdim and kollel yungeleit, should daven at least an hour and a half, everyone should daven longer on Shabbos, and whoever had time yet davened hastily would not be let in to hear the Rebbe's Torah. He notes that long davening is mocked, and brings the Gemara that before Moshiach the G-d-fearing will be called mad. Davening with the heart means the heart clings to every word, because, as the Chasam Sofer brings from the Ba'al Shem Tov, every word is a heichal. After a digression on how each chassid serves by his own root, he explains that stray thoughts mean being pushed out of Gan Eden. He then teaches that every day, and every person, has a unique task, as with Moshe Rabbeinu and Yosef HaTzaddik, and closes with preparing for the coming great days and for Moshiach.

en: In his letter, the Alter Rebbe asks that those who have time daven at least an hour and a half, and that everyone daven longer on Shabbos.
Davening with the heart means the heart is tied to every word, so that leaving a word is hard; understanding the words alone is davening with the head.
Every word of Torah and tefillah is a heichal, a piece of Gan Eden; stray thoughts during davening are a sign that one is being pushed out of it.
A chassid need not imitate his rebbe; each serves Hashem by the root of his soul, and what he receives from his rebbe is the point of avodah.
Every day brings its own task that will never return, and every person comes into the world for a particular moment of trial.
Great days are coming, and one must prepare a garment for greeting Moshiach, woven of Torah, mitzvos and tefillah.

chassidic paths and the root of the soul
the unique mission of each day

title.en: The Alter Rebbe's letter on long davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the first letter of Iggeres HaKodesh, sent to all the Alter Rebbe's shtiblach: those with time should daven at least an hour and a half, everyone longer on Shabbos, and appointed watchers would report anyone who hurried, who would then be barred from hearing the Rebbe's Torah.

title.en: Mocked for davening; davening with the heart

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that long davening is ridiculed and brings the Gemara that before Moshiach the G-d-fearing will be called mad. He explains 'ul'avdo b'chol levavchem' as davening where the heart clings to each word, and brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's teaching, cited by the Chasam Sofer, that every word is a heichal.

title.en: Each disciple serves by his own root

summary.en: Digressing, the Mashgiach explains that the Ba'al Shem Tov's disciples, and the many rebbes from the Rebbe of Lublin, each served Hashem differently; a true chassid does not imitate his rebbe but receives the point of avodah. He then returns to the Ba'al Shem Tov's teaching that every word of Torah and tefillah is a heichal.

title.en: Stray thoughts: pushed out of Gan Eden

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that stray thoughts in davening are being pushed out of Gan Eden, as Adam was after the sin, and that one who davens properly is let into the heichalos of Torah and tefillah. Such a person must daven longer, and his tears are tears of joy, like a parent and child reunited.

title.en: Every day and every person has a mission

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah set davening so that each day brings new light and its own tikkun, bringing Avraham 'ba bayamim', Hillel's 'if not now, when' and 'hamechadesh b'tuvo'. Every person comes for one moment of trial, like Moshe Rabbeinu for Matan Torah and Yosef, who became Yosef HaTzaddik through his test, so one must always be ready.

title.en: Preparing for great days and for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach says great days are coming, Adar and especially Nisan, that things are stirring in the world, and that one must prepare a garment for Moshiach woven of Torah, mitzvos and tefillah. He ends with a brachah that all merit to greet Moshiach unashamed; a niggun follows.

catalogTitle: “לא איש אל כל ויכזב” - Hashem Knows Past Present and Future

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Jewish emunah, which believes even what it cannot see, with Amalek's denial of what he saw, and shows from the Rambam and the pesukim that the Torah can never be changed, since Hashem is not a man who changes His mind.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by recalling that the Jewish belief in Moshe Rabbeinu and the Torah rests on what millions of Jews saw and heard at Har Sinai, passed down from generation to generation. Emunah in the full sense is believing what lies above human understanding, and since Hashem made the world with opposing forces, there is also a kefirah above understanding: denying what one sees. Amalek, who trembled at the splitting of the sea, still came to fight, the opposite of the Jews who believe even what they do not see. The Mashgiach then explains that the nations, Christians and Muslims, accept the Torah but cannot keep it, and so claim Hashem changed His mind. From the Rambam in Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah chapter nine and the pesukim, culminating in 'lo ish Kel vikazev', he shows the Torah can never change. He closes on why the nations hate the Jews, on censorship of sefarim, and on the security of Jewish emunah.

en: The Mashgiach says the Jewish belief in the Torah rests on what a whole nation saw and heard at Har Sinai and passed down, which cannot be questioned.
Emunah means believing what is above the intellect; opposite it stands a kefirah above the intellect, refusing to believe even what one sees.
Amalek, who trembled at the splitting of the sea along with the other chiefs of Edom, still came to fight, denying what he saw.
The nations accept the Torah but cannot keep it, so they rationalize that Hashem changed His mind and gave them another Torah.
The Rambam, from explicit pesukim, establishes that the Torah stands forever, may not be added to or reduced, and that any prophet who says otherwise is a false prophet.
Hashem does not change His mind, because He knows what will be later; the pasuk says He is not a man who lies or changes his mind.
The Mashgiach says the nations' hatred of the Jews comes from envy: deep down their thinking people know the truth but their pride and desires keep them from admitting it.

title.en: Emunah from Sinai and above the intellect

summary.en: The Mashgiach recalls that belief in Moshe Rabbeinu and the Torah rests on what millions saw and heard at Sinai and passed down. He mentions the coming season of Purim and the war against Amalek, then explains that emunah means believing what is above the intellect, and that Hashem made every force of holiness with an opposing force.

title.en: Amalek denies what he sees

summary.en: Opposite emunah above the intellect stands a kefirah above the intellect: refusing to believe what one sees. The Mashgiach explains that seeing is not believing, that the Jews at the sea believed even beyond what they saw, while Amalek, one of the terrified chiefs of Edom, came to fight anyway; Moshe Rabbeinu against Amalek is emunah against kefirah.

title.en: Why the nations accept the Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a fact witnessed by a multitude and passed down cannot be doubted, like the conquests of Alexander the Great, and the whole Jewish people everywhere has the same Torah and mitzvos. Therefore Christians and Muslims accept the Torah; he asks why they then have other religions and answers that they cannot keep it and rationalize that Hashem changed His mind.

title.en: The Torah can never change

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads from the Rambam, Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah chapter nine, that the Torah stands forever and nothing may be added or taken away, bringing the pesukim of 'lo sosef', 'lanu ul'vaneinu ad olam' and 'lo bashamayim hi'. A prophet who claims the mitzvos were temporary is a false prophet, and he ends with the pasuk that Hashem is not a man who lies or changes His mind, since He knows the future.

title.en: Why the nations hate the Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the learned among the nations know the truth but their pride and desires keep them from admitting it, and asks why they hate the Jews; he answers that it is envy. He describes how censors removed passages from the siddur, the Rambam and the Gemara, tells of converts who gave their lives for the truth, and closes with the security and joy of Jewish emunah in the Written and Oral Torah.

catalogTitle: בהירות בזמנינו כשיש הרבה בלבולי הדעת

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach tells bachurim that in the confusion of the final generation before Moshiach the main test is emunah, and, from Malachi's last prophecy, that those who fear Hashem must gather and strengthen one another.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that we stand in ikvesa d'meshicha, the 'heel' of the generations before Moshiach, facing a test like Avraham Avinu's last one, where the Satan argued convincingly and Avraham did not listen. Every soul was sent down from heaven on a mission, and he reads the first chapter of Mesilas Yesharim: man was created to delight in Hashem, and this world is only a corridor to the next. No one finds real happiness here, and a soul greater than the angels was not given for eating and drinking. The main test now is emunah, and he tells of the Slonimer Rebbe, the talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Ba'al Shem Tov himself. From the end of Malachi he shows that people will say serving Hashem does not pay, and the answer is that yirei Hashem speak to one another and strengthen each other. He ends with the Shabbos seudos, shalosh seudos and melave malka.

en: We are in the last stretch of ikvesa d'meshicha, and its test resembles Avraham Avinu's last test: not listening to the Satan even when his argument seems to make sense.
Following Mesilas Yesharim ch. 1, the Mashgiach teaches that man was created to delight in Hashem, and this world is only a corridor to the World to Come.
In the final period of galus the main test is emunah, as the passuk says, 'tzaddik be'emunaso yichyeh'.
Malachi, the last prophet, foretells that people will say serving Hashem does not pay, and gives the answer: those who fear Hashem speak to one another and strengthen each other.
The three Shabbos seudos rise in greatness like the three tefillos, and melave malka, Dovid HaMelech's seudah, corresponds to chatzos and draws the holiness of Shabbos into the week.

Ba'al Shem Tov and his talmidim

title.en: The heel of the generations and Avraham's last test

summary.en: The Mashgiach says we are at the very end of ikvesa d'meshicha, the lowest point of the generations, and that our test parallels Avraham Avinu's last test, where he did not listen to the Satan even though the Satan's argument seemed to make sense. Each Jew is an emissary of Hashem sent down for this.

title.en: The soul's mission and Mesilas Yesharim ch. 1

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the soul singing with the angels in heaven before it was sent down on a mission, and reads the opening of Mesilas Yesharim: the foundation of chassidus is knowing one's obligation in the world, that man was created to delight in Hashem, that this world is a corridor to the next, and that life here is one long battle.

title.en: No true happiness in this world

summary.en: Continuing Mesilas Yesharim, the Mashgiach says no one with sense can believe man was created for this world: even the richest and most powerful are full of troubles, competition and jealousy, and a soul greater than the angels was not needed for eating and playing. He then praises Mesilas Yesharim as a simple-looking sefer full of hidden depth.

title.en: Emunah as the test, and the Ba'al Shem Tov's talmidim

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the main test before Moshiach is emunah, and that davening must be elevated. He tells of the Slonimer Rebbe sensing a problem that a learned man explained away, asks how the Ba'al Shem Tov's talmidim could surpass the Amoraim, and brings the Satmar Rav's answer that they were souls of prophets sent as an exception to save the world.

title.en: Stories of the Ba'al Shem Tov

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells the Ruzhiner's story of how the Maggid trembled uncontrollably when he touched the Ba'al Shem Tov's garment during tefilas geshem, and how the Ba'al Shem Tov could only attend to worldly questions in the washroom, since his mind was always in heaven. He adds that the Ba'al Shem Tov's teacher was Achiya HaShiloni.

title.en: Malachi: 'serving Hashem does not pay'

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Malachi, the last prophet, speaks to the last generation about how to cross the sea of galus. He reads Malachi's closing words and the complaint of the people that serving Hashem is futile and the wicked prosper, and tells of bachurim at a yeshiva lunch table who said the same.

title.en: 'Az nidberu yirei Hashem': strengthening one another

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Malachi's answer for that time: those who fear Hashem gather and speak to one another to strengthen their emunah, Hashem listens and writes every word in a book of remembrance, and at the geulah everyone will see the difference between the tzaddik and the rasha.

title.en: Middos, shalosh seudos and melave malka

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why he agreed to meet the bachurim on Motzaei Shabbos for words of chizuk, stresses good middos, and compares the three Shabbos seudos to the three tefillos, each greater than the one before. Melave malka, Dovid HaMelech's seudah, corresponds to chatzos and brings Shabbos into the week; he closes with a brachah.

catalogTitle: חסידות -- עיקרים וטפלים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that holding on to emunah is an essence of Chassidus, that mockery is its opposite, and traces through history how every attempt to run away from the Ribono shel Olam failed, until the Ba'al Shem Tov revived the simple Jews.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that Chassidus is misunderstood today: it has roots and branches, and among its roots are seeking the truth and holding on to emunah, swimming against the current. Avraham Avinu dug wells of emunah, and the Plishtim stopped them up. A sefer teaches that the opposite of emunah is mockery, and the Mashgiach shows with a story of a boy who laughed at the Livyasan how one joke dismisses a hundred rebukes. That was how the Plishtim blocked Avraham's wells. He then follows the pattern through history: Mitzrayim, the exile, Yechezkel's warning that Jews cannot leave Hashem, the Haskalah in Germany, and Zionism, each meant to solve the Jews' troubles and each making them worse, illustrated with a parable of the animals' court. Jews kept their emunah through every persecution; after Shabsai Tzvi the Ba'al Shem Tov, a neshamah beyond his generation, raised up the simple Jews. He closes with stories of tzaddikim's sensitivity and of a chaburah that revived its listeners.

en: The Mashgiach says Chassidus is misunderstood today; among its great roots are seeking and knowing the truth and holding on to emunah.
Mockery is the opposite of emunah: one joke can dismiss a hundred rebukes, without any logic or argument.
The Plishtim stopped up Avraham Avinu's wells of emunah by mocking his greatness, and Yitzchak had to dig them again.
Every attempt to escape the Ribono shel Olam, from the exile in Yechezkel's time to the Haskalah and Zionism, failed and brought the Jews worse troubles.
Through every persecution Jews gave their lives for kiddush Hashem because they held on to emunah.
After the fall caused by Shabsai Tzvi, Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov, who raised up the simple Jews and showed them how precious they are to Hashem.

title.en: The roots of Chassidus: truth and emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Chassidus is misunderstood today, distinguishes its roots from its branches, and names seeking the truth and holding on to emunah as its essence. He introduces Avraham Avinu's wells of emunah and the Plishtim, and brings that mockery is the opposite of emunah.

title.en: One joke against a hundred rebukes

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a boy who mocked his teacher's words about the Livyasan, and explains how one joke dismisses a hundred rebukes. This was the Plishtim's way of stopping up Avraham's wells; he follows the pattern through Mitzrayim, Matan Torah and the exile, where Yechezkel warned that Jews cannot leave Hashem.

title.en: Haskalah, Zionism and the hope to end antisemitism

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the Haskalah in Germany, which promised that becoming like the gentiles would end antisemitism and instead led to the churban, and the Zionist idea of a homeland, first Uganda and then Eretz Yisroel. He notes that tzaddikim had first urged settling Eretz Yisroel, but refused to partner with the free Zionists.

title.en: The state and the parable of the sheep

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the Zionists succeeded beyond expectations, yet antisemitism became far worse, and the nations condemn the Jews for what every nation has done. He brings a vort on the last passuk of Tehillim 119 with a parable of the animals' court that excused the bear and the wolf and condemned the sheep, and concludes that nothing helps without the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: Mesirus nefesh in exile and the Ba'al Shem Tov

summary.en: The Mashgiach lists the generations of martyrdom, from the Ten Martyrs to the Crusades, the Inquisition and the decrees of 1648-49, all for emunah. After Shabsai Tzvi led many astray, Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov, who lifted up the simple Jews; the Mashgiach describes him as a neshamah beyond his generation, as the Gra was among the later authorities.

title.en: Stories of tzaddikim and a reviving chaburah

summary.en: The Mashgiach mentions that tzaddikim could sense forbidden food, and tells of the Belzer Rav at a tish who sensed that a crystal plate of grapes had not been toveled. He then recalls a Thursday chaburah in Williamsburg where stories of tzaddikim left the young men refreshed and eager to learn and daven.

catalogTitle: מטרת החסידות: להחזיק פשוטי עם באמונה: שמירת הקדושה: ואיחוד לבבות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Ba'al Shem Tov came to strengthen simple Jews in emunah, and that bachurim today must prepare for their tests through guarding kedushah and through love and unity among Jews despite their differences.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Ba'al Shem Tov's main aim: to strengthen simple Jews in emunah. Emunah is precious today, he says, and nobody knows what tests lie ahead. He tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov crossed a river on his belt and lit an icicle like a candle through emunah alone, and how he planted emunah and yiras Shamayim in the world. Just as the Avos prepared their children for Mitzrayim, the Ba'al Shem Tov's talmidim prepared later generations. Our generation is very low, and our task is to stay pure where it seems impossible. Before Moshiach there will be great tests, and for us they are small ones: guarding the eyes and thoughts, as Yosef did. A second kelipah today is machlokes between groups of ehrliche Jews. Different paths come from different roots, as R' Zeira stayed R' Yehudah's talmid and Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel loved each other. Bachurim must love every Jew who serves Hashem.

en: The Mashgiach says the Ba'al Shem Tov's main aim was to strengthen simple Jews, above all in emunah.
The Ba'al Shem Tov's wonders, crossing a river on his belt and lighting an icicle, came from emunah alone, not from holy names.
As the Avos prepared the Jews for galus Mitzrayim, the Ba'al Shem Tov and his talmidim prepared the later generations for their tests.
The great test before Moshiach is, for this generation, a matter of small things: not looking, not speaking lashon hara, guarding the eyes and thoughts.
Machlokes between ehrliche Jews over 'my Rebbe and your Rebbe' is a great kelipah of today and not what the Ba'al Shem Tov intended.
Just as every person's face is different, so are his opinions and his path; one may follow his own way and still love the other.

title.en: Emunah today and the Besht's river crossing

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to the Ba'al Shem Tov's aim of strengthening simple Jews in emunah, notes how many come to him today with questions of emunah, and says nobody knows what tests lie ahead. He tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov crossed a great river standing on his belt, through emunah alone.

title.en: The burning icicle and seeing the soul's root

summary.en: From Shivchei HaBesht the Mashgiach tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov lit an icicle like a candle on a cold night, comparing it to Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa. He adds the Belzer Rav's saying that every ehrliche Jew in Germany came from the Ba'al Shem Tov, and how the Maggid could see a soul's root down to the earth Adam was made from.

title.en: Preparing the generations, and our low state

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares the Besht's talmidim to the Avos, who prepared the Jews for Mitzrayim; the tests of Yosef and Sarah gave Jewish men and women the strength to stay pure. He describes today's impurity entering homes, brings the Midrash on 'b'goy naval', and the Satan's task with Iyov, to break the barrel but keep the wine, as the picture of our task.

title.en: The tests before Moshiach are small things

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells what a tzaddik in Yerushalayim, Rabbi Eliyahu Roth, foretold about Russia and the year 2000, and stresses that nobody can know the time; one must be ready for every test. A test is when one doesn't know the outcome, like Avraham at the Akeidah, and for this generation the tests are small: not looking out of curiosity, not speaking lashon hara.

title.en: Kedushas einayim and pure thoughts

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Chanukah's lights train the eyes, so that one merits 'ki ayin b'ayin yiru'. A stray thought is not a sin; keeping it is, as the Bnei Yissaschar writes. Yosef was called tzaddik for guarding himself; this middah is called yesod, and failing in it can cost a person his tzelem Elokim and his taste for Shabbos.

title.en: The kelipah of machlokes; each path has its root

summary.en: The Mashgiach names a second kelipah, machlokes among ehrliche Jews over 'my Rebbe, your Rebbe', brings the Divrei Chaim on the erev rav, and says the Besht never meant this. The Maggid's talmidim each went their own way, and minhagim differ even between cousins; he brings R' Zeira, who differed with R' Yehudah about Eretz Yisroel yet stayed his talmid.

title.en: Different faces, one love

summary.en: The Mashgiach says pirud halevavos is among the great kelipos today and calls on bachurim to love every Jew who serves Hashem. As faces differ, so do opinions, like dollar bills from one plate versus people from Adam's mold; Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel loved each other. He mentions Emunas Yisroel taking good points from everywhere, the Besht's shared seudos, and sums up the two topics: shmiras hakedushah and unity.

catalogTitle: “וצדיק באמונתו יחיה” - The Mitzvah of the Last Generation

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Habakkuk placed the whole Torah on the one mitzvah of emunah because the last generation, the 'heel' of Adam HaRishon, must concentrate its strength on emunah, which is its special mission.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara in Makkos that the nevi'im reduced the 613 mitzvos until Habakkuk placed the whole Torah on one: 'the tzaddik lives by his emunah.' This does not free anyone from the other mitzvos; it means a small generation must concentrate on one mitzvah. To explain, he brings the Midrash that all souls were contained in Adam HaRishon, and that the generations together form one body. The generation of the desert was the head, devoted to Torah; later generations with the Beis HaMikdash were the heart, the masters of tefillah, led by Moshe Rabbeinu and David HaMelech respectively. Our generation is the heel: low, without sensitivity, in the dark. The Mashgiach also warns that machlokes can spoil a year fit for Moshiach, as the Chasam Sofer said of an earlier generation. Every soul has a mission, known by a strong desire for it and by the obstacles the Satan puts in its way. Today's mission is emunah, which is why the whole world now works against it.

en: Habakkuk's placing the Torah on emunah does not mean one may drop the other mitzvos; it means the last generation must concentrate on this one mitzvah.
All souls were contained in Adam HaRishon, each attached to a particular limb, and a person functions according to the place his soul came from.
The generations together form one body: the generation of the desert is the head, the generations of the Beis HaMikdash are the heart, and our generation is the heel.
Like the heel, our generation lacks sensitivity and stays in the dark, which is why there is so much blindness and so many Jews going astray.
Every soul is sent down on a particular mission, recognized by two signs: a strong desire for it and the obstacles that make it hard.
Since the mission of today is emunah, the Satan has arranged the whole world to take emunah away.

title.en: Habakkuk's one mitzvah and Adam HaRishon's soul

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Makkos on how the nevi'im reduced the mitzvos until Habakkuk placed the Torah on emunah, and explains that this means concentrating on one mitzvah, since earlier great souls could give themselves to every mitzvah and we are small. He then brings the Midrash that all souls were in Adam HaRishon, attached to different limbs, and that the generations form one such body.

title.en: The head and the heart of the generations

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the generation of the desert was the head, a congregation of Torah and intellect led by Moshe Rabbeinu, while the generations of the Beis HaMikdash were the heart, the masters of tefillah led by David HaMelech. A person from the head or the heart can choose to turn that strength to Torah or tefillah, or to other fields; the hands are perhaps the givers of tzedakah.

title.en: Our generation is the heel

summary.en: The Mashgiach says our generation is the heel of Adam HaRishon. He interrupts to warn that the machlokes now prevalent may spoil a year fit for Moshiach, as the Chasam Sofer said of the great generation of the Yaavetz and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz. Then he explains that like the sole of the foot, our generation has no sensitivity and is always in the dark, hence the blindness and the Jews going astray.

title.en: The mitzvah of the last generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Gemara's name for the last generation, 'ikvesa deMeshicha', carries the sense of the heel and of shame, and that it is for this generation that Habakkuk placed everything on emunah. He says one must live with emunah, learn, think and talk about it, and introduces the idea that every soul has a mission the Satan tries to block.

title.en: Two signs of one's mission; the war on emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach gives two signs of a person's mission: a strong desire, as every creature desires what it needs, and obstacles placed by the Satan, as with rising early to learn and daven. Since today's mission is emunah, the Satan has turned the whole world against it; he tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov left a wagon whose driver showed no faith, and says that having no belief at all is worse than false belief.

catalogTitle: חשיבות העבודה בחושך

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that avodah done in a dark time like Teves, or in a dark place, is especially precious above, and then turns to how bachurim should go to sleep on time so as to rise fresh for avodah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by urging that the light of Chanukah be carried into the dark month of Teves with hasmadah and bright tefillos, turning darkness to light. Citing Sefer Yetzirah, he shows that place, time and soul mirror each other: Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol and the Kodesh HaKodashim meet. The same holds for impurity, which has its place, its person and its time, Nittel, when the custom is not to learn. He brings the Gemara of Onkelos and the Bnei Yissaschar's explanation of the punishment of false wisdom. Yet Teves is also when great gems can be found in the depths, as in the parable of the pearl placed at the head of the king's crown. Following the Kedushas Levi, every time contains all times. The second half turns to rising early, kerias shema before sleep, sleep as avodah and a kind of techiyas hamesim, and going to sleep on time.

en: The Mashgiach says that by bringing the light of Chanukah into Teves with hasmadah, Torah and bright tefillos, and with simcha, one turns the darkness into light.
Place, time and soul parallel one another; this holds for holiness and also for impurity, which has its place, its person and its time, Nittel.
Avodah done in a dark time or a dark place is valued in Heaven like the avodah of great tzaddikim, as the pearl from the dark depths was set at the head of the king's crown.
Following the Kedushas Levi, every time contains all times, so a Jew's avodah in Teves can awaken Pesach, Shavuos or Sukkos.
Sleep is part of avodas Hashem: in sleep the soul ascends and is strengthened, and sleep is a kind of techiyas hamesim from which a person rises a new creation.
The Mashgiach says one must go to sleep early and on time, sleep as much as one truly needs to be alert, and not linger in bed past that.
